# 767: THE RUNG-24 ARM - `armed-storage-94de2ede`, STAGE90_XNU_STORAGE_PROBE=23.
# Built 2026-09-27 host-side only: NO device action, NO press, NO gate against a
# device, NO runner. It is 766's rung-23 window PLUS ONE NEW CELL, and the cell
# costs no device access at all: the poll that already reads PRESENT_STATE 0x24
# once per iteration into `inhibit_last` now also counts the samples in which bit
# 24 (the CMD line's own LEVEL) is LOW. `_nidx_cmdlow_seen = 0` over the same
# first 1024 samples `_nidx_inhibit_seen` counts is the reading that separates
# 764 section 4's candidate 3 (the block never drove the bus) from candidate 1
# (the block drove and the card stayed silent) - the one question no arm in this
# ladder has ever been able to ask, because `_nidx_inhibit_last` is the LAST
# sample and an idle line and a finished transmission both read HIGH.
#
# **`out/` NOW HOLDS THIS ARM, AND `armed-storage-3a92aa52` (rung 23) IS NO
# LONGER IN `out/`** - its park is intact and unchanged (11 members, every one
# cmp-identical to what 766 parked), so rung 23 can still be re-armed with
# `tools/verify_revert_set.sh out/stage90/frozen/armed-storage-3a92aa52 --set=armed-storage-3a92aa52`.
# NO PRESS IS SPENT BY THIS STEP AND NONE IS AUTHORIZED.
#
# What did NOT move, measured on the new artifacts rather than asserted:
# `entry_epilogue` is still 0x80004948 and STAGE90_XNU_SEAM_LR is still
# 0x800492dc (the build's own seam clause, exit 0); `xnu_arm_entry.bin` is
# 5552764 bytes, unchanged, the growth having fitted the padding; and the
# payload switch set is BYTE-IDENTICAL to rung 23's (6c2b6038...), which is the
# trap 763 section 5 and 766 section 6 paid for.
#
# `st_send_command`'s device set is UNCHANGED BY THIS RUNG, and that was
# MEASURED rather than argued: the classifier reports
# `f9824924:ldr f9824930:ldr f9824930:str f9824908:str f982490e:strh
#  f982490e:ldrh f9824910:ldr` and an image-side set of exactly
# `UNK:ldr UNK:str` - the same pair rung 11's clause names. So the census added
# no register, no width and no new symbol. **A relaxation of that clause was
# drafted, and REMOVED after this measurement showed it was not needed**: it
# would have weakened a load-bearing check for a reason that was not true.

# 768: THE RUNG-24 PRESS - `armed-storage-94de2ede` WAS PRESSED AND IT ANSWERED.
# ONE PRESS SPENT, WITH THE OPERATOR'S AUTHORIZATION, 2026-09-27 09:05:22-09:06:36
# UTC (74 s), EXIT 0, returned and captured. One `fastboot boot` only, never
# flash; neighbour `33e80afe` absent from BOTH `adb devices` and `fastboot devices`
# at fire time (`4a2fe00b` present as `device`); exactly one gate
# (`--allow-xnu-entry`, exit 0, 600 lines) and exactly one runner
# (`--allow-xnu-entry --expect-arm=armed-storage-94de2ede`), both with the flags
# readiness printed; readiness 5 of 5 beforehand. Capture archived by hand
# (the runner does not archive) as
# `out/stage90/captures/rung24-cmdline-20260927-090636-last_kmsg.txt`, 631,581 B,
# sha256 053818944ec8009f55e1ebeded90c82b45cdaa24861e2fe6e9d4013d130c506e, with
# its `-gate.log` and `-run.log` companions.
#
# **THE ANSWER IS ROW 1 OF THE PRE-REGISTERED FOUR-ROW TABLE.** `_nidx_status_any
# = 0x00018000` = `SDHCI_INT_ERROR` (bit 15) + `SDHCI_INT_TIMEOUT` (bit 16),
# `_nidx_err = 0x00010000`, `_nidx_complete = 0`, `_nidx_timeout = 0` (a break at
# poll 1789, not the 1.2 s budget), `_nidx_ticks = 0x31e3` = 12,771 ticks =
# **665.2 us** - THE CARD DID NOT ANSWER AND THE CONTROLLER KNEW IT.
#
# **AND THE 665 us IS THE TIMEOUT'S OWN SIGNATURE**: `TIMEOUT_CONTROL 0x2E` read
# 0, value 0 = 2^13 TMCLK cycles, and 8192 / 665.2 us = 12.31 MHz against this
# platform's 12.288 MHz - **666.7 us predicted, 665.2 us measured**.
#
# **AND THE CMD LINE MOVED**: `_nidx_cmdlow_seen = 0x187` = 391 of the first 1024
# samples, so 764 section 4's candidate 3 (the block never put anything on the
# bus) is RETIRED; candidate 2 (the response timeout not armed) is retired by the
# 665 us itself.
#
# **THE LARGER RESULT IS IN THE SAME LOG FROM RUNG 11**: `_cmd0_complete = 1` and
# `_cmd0_status_any = 0x00000001` (`SDHCI_INT_RESPONSE`) at poll 537 in 255.4 us.
# A no-response command completes and says so; a response-demanding one is
# issued, drives the line, and arms and FIRES its own timeout. **THE RUNGS-13-22
# HEADLINE - "this controller runs a command and never sets its status" - IS
# FALSE**, and it was false because the error-enable half of `INT_ENABLE 0x34`
# was zero. 765's mask finding is confirmed one cell deeper:
# `_nidx_status_pre = 0x00018000` (INT_STATUS read between the enable store and
# its readback) shows a timeout summary LATCHED AND INVISIBLE since an earlier
# command. Two producers - named as m739's shape - and the poll settles the fresh
# latch independently: `_nidx_clear_after = 0`, then a break at poll 1789.
#
# Safety, cell by cell: `_nidx_sig_enable = 0` (SIGNAL_ENABLE never written) and
# NO `_irq_other_*` key anywhere in the log - no delivery reached the dispatcher;
# `_nidx_ena_held = 0x000f8001`, `_nidx_readback = 0x00008000`; all
# `persistent_write_attempted` and `failure_mask` zero; ending unmoved
# (`_post_end_calls = 6`, `_seam_sctlr = 0x30c57879`, `_sleh_storm = 9`).
#
# **WHAT IS LEFT.** The controller is exonerated. The candidate space is the
# card's power and the clock at its pins - the two things a register read of the
# controller cannot see. Host-side, three obvious suspicions are CLOSED: the
# 1.8 V power byte is correct (`_pwr_wrote = 0x0b` = `SDHCI_POWER_180|ON`, from
# CAPABILITIES 0x742dc8b2's VDD_180-only, and the board's
# `qcom,vdd-io-voltage-level = <1800000 1800000>` agrees); the `qcom,pad-*`
# settings are drive strength and pull and NOT a function mux; and HOST_CONTROL's
# bus width cannot matter for data-less commands.
#
# **m776 - a field's DIRECTION stated backwards in a live instruction.**
# `TIMEOUT_CONTROL`'s `0x00` was called the field's LONGEST setting in 765
# section 4 and carried into 766 and into BOTH the rung-23 and rung-24 readiness
# narrations. It is the SHORTEST (value v selects 2^(13+v) TMCLK cycles), and
# this press measured it. The correction in `src/entry/entry_storage.c` is OWED,
# not paid: that file is one of the entry image's 23 recorded sources, so editing
# its `#error` text makes the gate refuse the arm this press just spent (763
# section 5's measured cost). It is corrected in the experiment document and in
# `tools/verify_press_ready.sh`, which is not an entry source.
#
# **RUNG 23's PARK IS NOW SUPERSEDED AND UNSPENT.** `armed-storage-3a92aa52`'s
# question is answered by this press, and its park stays intact and verified.
# NO PRESS IS OWED AND NONE IS AUTHORIZED; `out/` still holds this arm, pressed.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 769: THE SDC1 PADS - HOST-SIDE ONLY. NO DEVICE ACTION, NO PRESS, NO ARM BUILT,
# NO GATE AGAINST A DEVICE, NO RUNNER, NO FIRER. `out/` is untouched: the live
# arm is still 768's spent `armed-storage-94de2ede`, and rung 23's
# `armed-storage-3a92aa52` remains a superseded, unspent park. Nothing in this
# block was measured on hardware; every claim carries its `file:line`.
#
# **768 SECTION 5's *FUNCTION MUX* IS RETIRED BY CONSTRUCTION.** MSM8974 routes
# SDC1 through DEDICATED PADS, not GPIOs: `sdhci-msm.c:267-270` documents the
# distinction and `sdhci-msm.c:1266` picks the pad branch because `sdhc_1` has no
# `gpios` property; `sdhci_msm_setup_pad` (`sdhci-msm.c:964-988`) calls only
# `msm_tlmm_set_hdrive`/`msm_tlmm_set_pull`, both landing in `MSM_TLMM_BASE`
# (phys 0xFD510000, `msm_iomap-8974.h:34-35`) at `SDC1_HDRV_PULL_CTL = 0x2044`
# -> **0xFD512044**. Every field of that register is drive strength or pull
# (`gpio-msm-common.c:59-88`); there is no function-select field to write. The
# function-select writers that exist in this tree are applied only to the
# GPIO-routed SDC3/SDC4.
#
# **THE VENDOR WRITES THE PADS FROM INSIDE THE POWER ISR.** `sdhci_msm_pwr_irq`'s
# `CORE_PWRCTL_BUS_ON` branch (`sdhci-msm.c:2015-2032`) does
# `sdhci_msm_setup_vreg` -> `sdhci_msm_setup_pins` -> `sdhci_msm_set_vdd_io_vol`.
# Rung 7 wrote the power byte and rung 8 registered the handler, but the ladder's
# handler acks the latch rather than performing the vendor's BUS_ON work, so
# **the pads' drive and pull have been attempted by no rung.**
#
# **THE PRE-REGISTERED EXPECTED VALUE.** `msm8974pro-ac-pm8941-mtp-v5.dts:25-29`
# gives `&sdhc_1` `qcom,pad-pull-on = <0x0 0x3 0x3 0x1>` and
# `qcom,pad-drv-on = <0x4 0x4 0x4>`; through `msm_tlmm_set_field`'s
# `reg &= ~(mask<<off); reg |= (val&mask)<<off;` (`gpio-msm-common.c:481-496`)
# that evaluates field by field to **0x00009F24**. The field that is the
# mechanism is `PULL SDC1_CMD = pull-up`: MMC's CMD line is OPEN-DRAIN during
# identification and returns HIGH only through this pull, which on this SoC is
# the pad register rather than a discrete resistor. A board left at reset reads
# 0x00000000 - no pull-up on CMD, no pull-up on DATA.
#
# **NEXT ARM PRE-REGISTERED, NOT BUILT.** Install the 0xFD5 megabyte through
# `entry_mmio_section` (693's design; 0xFD512044 >> 20 = 0xFD5 and no other
# device lives there, so 692's `addr >> 20` interlock is satisfied by
# construction), then ONE 32-bit read, ZERO stores, published raw as `_pad_raw`
# beside seven field decodes plus `_pad_map` and `_pad_writes = 0`.
# ROW 1: `0x00009F24` -> the pads are configured, 768 section 5's other half is
# retired, and the subject moves to the PMIC rails (`sdhci_msm_setup_vreg`, a bus
# the ladder cannot reach from `hc_mem`).
# ROW 2: `0x00000000`, or any field at odds with the DT -> the vendor act was
# never applied on this path, and the next rung is a single read-modify-write of
# one register whose section is already installed.
#
# **THREE CANDIDATES RETIRED AND ONE CONTRADICTION FOUND IN 768.**
# (i) `HOST_CONTROL2 0x3E` bit 3 `VDD_180` = 0 is NOT a defect:
# `sdhci_msm_set_uhs_signaling` read-modify-writes only `UHS_MASK`
# (`sdhci-msm.c:2544-2546`, `:2597`), and the only writer of `VDD_180` is
# `sdhci_do_start_signal_voltage_switch` (`sdhci.c:2015`), called on timing
# switches and not at 400 kHz init. The vendor's own HOST_CONTROL2 is 0 at the
# first command too.
# (ii) 768 section 1's mechanism attribution is a coincidence read as causation:
# `SDHCI_INT_TIMEOUT` (`sdhci.h:130`) is the COMMAND timeout, and `sdhci.c`
# writes `TIMEOUT_CONTROL 0x2E` only at `:115` (a dump) and `:828` (inside
# `if (data || (cmd->flags & MMC_RSP_BUSY))` at `:826`). No ladder command
# carries either, so the register is at its RESET value and *unset* and *set to
# longest* are indistinguishable when the field is 0. The 665.2 us against
# 2^13 @ 12.288 MHz = 666.7 us is still a real reading - and a positive
# measurement that TMCLK runs - but the attribution is not.
# (iii) 768 section 3's "the RESPONSE register was read and never changed" is
# refuted by the arm's own cells: `_nidx_resp_pre = 0` -> `_nidx_resp` =
# `_nidx_resp_post` = 0x40ff8080 with `_nidx_resp_moved = 1`, and the pre-words
# at +12/+8 (0x0040ff80 / 0x80000000) went to zero. All three reads are
# `ST_SDHCI_RESPONSE 0x10`, so the change is about ONE register.
#
# **AND THE CONTRADICTION IS SETTLED HOST-SIDE, WITH NO PRESS.** Rung 20's
# archived capture carries a CMD3 with `_nrsp_flags = 0x00000000`
# (`MMC_RSP_NONE`) and `_nrsp_resp_moved = 1` (0x40ff8080 -> 0): **a command that
# demanded nothing moves the register.** So the movement is the block's own and
# **RESPONSE is retired as a cell about the card in BOTH directions** - rung 19
# 0x40ff8080->0, rung 20 0x40ff8080->0, rung 24 0->0x40ff8080, the direction
# tracking the field's prior content and not what the command asked for.
#
# **A CENSUS CLAIM RECORDED AS WRONG SO IT IS NOT CARRIED.** A reading of the
# vendor bring-up pass produced "the vendor writes 0x29 = 0x0E | 0x01 = 0x0F, VDD
# 3.3 V". It is false: `sdhci_set_power` switches on `1 << power` where `power =
# ios->vdd` is a BIT INDEX (`sdhci.c:1312-1318`); `ocr_avail = MMC_VDD_165_195`
# because `CAPABILITIES 0x742dc8b2` has CAN_VDD_330/CAN_VDD_300 clear and
# CAN_VDD_180 set (`sdhci.h:195-197`; `sdhci.c:3434/3447/3460`); `fls(ocr_avail)
# - 1 = 7` -> `SDHCI_POWER_180 = 0x0A` -> **0x0B**, which is what the ladder
# writes. The wrong claim came from reading the storage assignment
# `sdhci.c:1339 host->pwr = pwr` without evaluating the switch above it - m737's
# shape: a claim about a REGISTER that is really a claim about a MOMENT.
#
# **NO PRESS SPENT, NO ARM BUILT, NO PRESS OWED AND NONE AUTHORIZED.** The goal
# is still NOT met - no storage, no filesystem, no mount - and TWRP-to-storage
# stays withheld.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 770: THE RUNG-25 ARM - `armed-storage-f72e9f18`, STAGE90_XNU_STORAGE_PROBE=24.
# Built 2026-09-27 host-side only: NO device action, NO press, NO gate against a
# device, NO runner, NO firer. It is 769 section 6's pre-registration made real,
# and it is the smallest arm this ladder has ever carried: **ONE READ, ONE NEW
# MEGABYTE, ZERO STORES.**
#
# WHAT IT IS. `st_pad_census` installs the 0xFD5 megabyte through
# `entry_mmio_section` (693's design; 692's press is why the install comes
# before the dereference - an uninstalled megabyte faults with fsr = 0x5), then
# takes ONE 32-bit read of `0xFD512044` - `TLMM + 0x2044`, the SDC1
# dedicated-pad drive/pull register, in a SECOND device's megabyte that no rung
# in this ladder has ever read or written. It publishes the word raw as
# `xnu_live_storage_pad_raw` beside seven field decodes (clk/cmd/data drive at
# bits 6/3/0, clk/cmd/data/rclk pull at 13/11/9/15), the derived expectation
# `xnu_live_storage_pad_expect = 0x00009F24`, a one-bit `_pad_match`, the
# `entry_mmio_section` outcome (`_pad_map`, `_pad_slot_before`, `_pad_desc`) and
# **`xnu_live_storage_pad_writes = 0`, a count that never leaves zero.**
#
# THE EXPECTATION IS DERIVED AND NOT TYPED. `qcom,pad-pull-on = <0x0 0x3 0x3 0x1>`
# and `qcom,pad-drv-on = <0x4 0x4 0x4>` (`msm8974pro-ac-pm8941-mtp-v5.dts:25-29`)
# through `msm_tlmm_set_field`'s shift-and-mask (hdrive width 3, pull width 2,
# `gpio-msm-common.c:481-496`) evaluate to 0x00009F24, and six `_Static_assert`s
# in `entry_storage.c` fix the address (== 0xfd512044), its megabyte
# (`>> 20 == 0xFD5`), its alignment, the seven masks' disjointness (their sum
# equals their OR) and that the expectation ANDs with the CMD-pull mask - so the
# value the arm compares against is computed from the DT arrays on every build
# rather than pasted from this paragraph.
#
# THE TWO-ROW ANSWER, PRE-REGISTERED IN 769 SECTION 6 AND UNCHANGED:
# ROW 1: `_pad_raw = 0x00009F24` -> THE PADS ARE CONFIGURED. 768 section 5's
#        other half is retired, `PULL SDC1_CMD` is present, and the subject moves
#        to the PMIC rails - `sdhci_msm_setup_vreg` (`sdhci-msm.c:2019`), a bus
#        the ladder cannot reach from `hc_mem`.
# ROW 2: `_pad_raw = 0x00000000`, or any field at odds with the DT -> THE VENDOR
#        ACT WAS NEVER APPLIED ON THIS PATH: no pull-up on CMD, no pull-up on
#        DATA, drive strength at minimum. The next rung is then a single
#        read-modify-write of ONE register in a megabyte whose section this arm
#        has already installed.
# ONE CAVEAT THE CELL CANNOT CARRY, recorded with it: the read is taken at the
# arm's own moment, which is BEFORE the command path, so row 1 is a reading about
# the pads' STATE and not a proof that this image applied them - the boot chain
# may have left exactly the same values. Only row 2 carries an act.
#
# **THE SEAM CONSTANT MOVED A FOURTH TIME AND THE BUILD REFUSED IT.**
# `st_pad_census` and its call site grew `entry_storage.o` past the entry group's
# remaining alignment slack, so the whole kernel text run moved by one page and
# the exit's `bl FlushPoU_Dcache` is now at **0x8004a2d8** returning to
# **0x8004a2dc** (`0x800492d8` -> `0x800492dc` on 724's arm, which is the value
# every arm from 724 to 768 carried). The build refused with its own clause -
# `the exit's call to FlushPoU_Dcache is at 2147787480 and returns to 2147787484,
# while entry_trace.c's STAGE90_XNU_SEAM_LR is 0x800492dc` - and after the refusal
# BOTH copies of the address were moved: `entry_trace.c:2688`'s
# `STAGE90_XNU_SEAM_LR` and `scripts/run_and_capture.sh:315`'s
# `EXIT_POP_LR_LITERAL`, which `preflight_boot_check.sh` compares against the live
# ELF ([[mi4-one-value-two-definitions]]). **The mechanism is the one 696, 708 and
# 724 measured: the move is a page, and it is a property of the entry group's SIZE
# and not of what a rung does.** `platform_cache_idle_enter` is now
# 0x8004a238..0x8004a2d4 and the entry's window is [0x8004a240, 0x8004a33c).
#
# **A REFUSED ENTRY BUILD LEAVES `out/` IN A STATE WORTH NAMING.** The entry
# build writes `xnu_arm_entry.bin` BEFORE its clause family runs, so the refused
# rung-25 build left a new entry bin (`594d539ae41f28da…`) sitting beside the
# rung-24 arm's own config record (`94de2ede…`, 08:54) - a pair the record does
# not describe and the gate's blob clause refuses. The live ARM was never in
# doubt (`stage90-qcdt.img` was untouched, still 94de2ede's), but **the lesson is
# that a refused entry build must be finished or re-armed from a park before any
# press**: `out/` is not left as it was.
#
# WHAT DID NOT MOVE, MEASURED ON THE NEW ARTIFACTS RATHER THAN ASSERTED:
# `xnu_arm_entry.bin` is 5552764 bytes, unchanged - the growth fitted the padding
# while the page boundary inside it was still crossed. The payload's switch set is
# BYTE-IDENTICAL to rung 24's and rung 23's (`6c2b6038...`, `stage90-build-config.txt`,
# 682 bytes, with `STAGE90_XNU_ENTRY 1` at line 5), which is the trap 763 section 5
# paid for and `tools/check_payload_config_entry.sh` now refuses. The build's own
# rung-25 clause reports the body's device set as `[fd512044:ldr ]` with counts
# `[fd512044:ldr=1 ]` and an EMPTY image side, in program order, called once from
# `entry_storage_probe` before `st_cmd_path` - so the arm's safety reading is the
# build's reading and not this paragraph's.

#   docs/experiments/experiment-771-the-command-table-read-as-one-table.md - the reading itself, with the

# 783: THE MASK THE LADDER FOUND WAS LIFTED AT ONE OF THREE WINDOWS - CMD1's and CMD2's still run with

#   THE SENTENCE THIS FOLLOWS. 765 section 1 measured that the vendor's own `sdhci_init` writes ELEVEN
#   bits (0x01FF0003) into INT_ENABLE 0x34 and drew: *"if the latch is enable-gated, a poll over a

#     3110  st_all_send_cid      CMD2              int_enable | ST_SDHCI_INT_RESPONSE  -> 0x00000001
#     3981  st_cmd3_noidx        CMD3              ena (built :3976 under #if >= 22)    -> 0x000f0001
#   and the tool's own summary: the FIVE-BIT word is built at ONE line and reaches ONE store, all in

#   WHAT IT MEANS FOR THE ARMED PRESS. In the rung-28 arm CMD1's and CMD2's windows still run with
#   INT_ENABLE = 0x00000001, so their _status_any = 0 over the full 1.2 s is STILL THE MASKED READING
#   765 described - on this arm the mask was lifted for the LAST command and left standing for the two
#   that run FIRST. CMD1 is SEND_OP_COND, the command an eMMC must answer for the ladder to move at all.
#   THE PRESS WOULD ANSWER THE PAD QUESTION AND THE CMD-LINE COUNTS AND LEAVE THE CMD1 TIMEOUT QUESTION
#   WHERE RUNG 21 LEFT IT --- not a reason not to spend it (row 1 of the pad fork closes a candidate on

# 782: THE ARMED FORK IS A TABLE WITH FOUR ROWS - the same declarations name the register's OFF state,
# and a two-row fork merges it with "never applied". HOST-SIDE ONLY: no device action, no press, no gate

#   `drv-off [0, 0, 0]` -> **0x00009E00**, the PULL HALF OF 0x9F24 WITH THE DRIVE HALF ZEROED. The three
#   words differ ONLY in the three hdrive fields: 0x00009F24 = 0x9E00 | 0x124 (4/4/4), 0x00009FE4 =
#   0x9E00 | 0x1E4 (7/4/4), 0x00009E00 = 0x9E00 | 0x000 (0/0/0).

#   SO `_pad_raw` IS A FOUR-ROW READING AND NOT A TWO-ROW FORK: 0x9F24 -> the pads are at the vendor's
#   CORE_PWRCTL_BUS_ON state; 0x9FE4 -> configured to the OTHER declared board's word; **0x9E00 -> the
#   PULLS ARE PRESENT AND THE DRIVE IS OFF**, a state no BUS_ON leaves, whose pull half is IDENTICAL to
#   row 1's, so 769 section 2's missing-pull-up mechanism is RETIRED on this row too and a fork that
#   calls it "the vendor act was never applied" merges it with row 4; 0x00000000 or anything else -> a
#   state NO declaration in this archive produces, the row that would say a bootloader used its own
#   values. On row 3 the three hdrive fields stay the subject; on row 4 the pull fields are zero and the
#   mechanism is live.
#
#   LANDED AS A CHECK AND NOT A SENTENCE. tools/derive_sdc1_pads.py derives and prints the OFF words
#   (via `derive_or_none`, which returns NONE for an array shorter than the field list rather than

#   record carries an OFF-word column per tree and one machine-readable `# offword 0x00009e00 ...` line;
#   and tools/check_sdc1_pad_expectation.py REFUSES a guard constant equal to an off word, because the

#   arithmetic alone (both ON words, the OFF word, and the three short/absent array shapes that must

# 780: THE VENDOR'S OWN PATH POWERS THE CARD - the reason this record gave for closing 764 section 3's
# power candidate is a driver reading that does not apply to this board. HOST-SIDE ONLY: no device action,
# no press, no gate, no runner, no firer, nothing built, and `out/` is byte-identical before and after -
# the armed rung-28 arm (armed-storage-d5d98738) is unspent. Every vendor line below was read in the
# checkout at external/android_kernel_xiaomi_cancro/, which `.gitignore:12` excludes.
#
#   THE TWO HALVES OF THE SENTENCE AT 5644. (1) TRUE: `sdhci.c:3583-3587` does `regulator_get(mmc_dev(mmc),
#   "vmmc")`, the DT supplies `vdd-supply`, so it takes IS_ERR, prints "no vmmc regulator found" and sets
#   `host->vmmc = NULL`, and every `mmc_regulator_set_ocr` is guarded by `host->vmmc &&` (`:1625`, `:1667`,
#   `:1688`, `:1833`) - verified, and re-verified in 780. (2) FALSE: "The vendor does not turn the card's
#   power on either." `host->vmmc` is `sdhci.c`'s OWN rail handle. `sdhci-msm.c` - the driver that binds
#   `sdhc_1` (`compatible = "qcom,sdhci-msm"`; the legacy `sdcc1` node is `status = "disabled"`,
#   `msm8974-mtp.dtsi:368-370`) - has its own vreg table from the SAME node's `vdd-supply`/`vdd-io-supply`
#   and its own path, read end to end:
#     sdhci_msm_probe:2826        sdhci_msm_vreg_init(&pdev->dev, msm_host->pdata, true)
#     sdhci_msm_vreg_init:1873    is_init true -> vreg_init_reg(h) per rail (regulator_get)
#                                 -> sdhci_msm_vreg_reset(pdata)
#     sdhci_msm_vreg_reset:1861   setup_vreg(pdata, 1, true)   <-- ENABLE
#                                 setup_vreg(pdata, 0, true)
#     sdhci_msm_vreg_enable:1765  regulator_enable(vreg->reg)   <-- NO is_always_on TEST
#   So on any Linux boot of this board `regulator_enable()` runs on BOTH `pm8941_l20` and `pm8941_s3`.
#
#   AND `qcom,vdd-always-on` DOES NOT CAUSE THE EARLY RETURN THIS BLOCK ALSO LEANS ON. That return's own
#   comment (`:1834-1836`) says "vreg info unavailable, assuming the slot is powered by always on domain",
#   and the phrase is what made it look like the property's effect. The guard is `if (!curr_slot)` on
#   `pdata->vreg_data`, and `vreg_data == NULL` CANNOT HAPPEN on a DT-bound device: `populate_pdata:1397`
#   allocates it UNCONDITIONALLY, before parsing anything, and `goto out`s only on allocation failure;
#   the per-rail parse (`:1060-1064`) returns early - leaving that rail NULL - only when the `-supply`
#   phandle is MISSING, and this board declares both. The flag's ONLY behavioural consumer is in the
#   RELEASE path: `:1072-1074` sets `is_always_on` from `qcom,%s-always-on`, `vreg_disable:1796` skips
#   `regulator_disable` when it is set, and `:1813-1817` demotes to LPM instead (and `qcom,vdd-lpm-sup` is
#   declared at `msm8974-mtp.dtsi:389`). **`always_on` means ENABLE IT AND NEVER RELEASE IT - the opposite
#   of "skip the regulator call".**
#
#   THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES, AND ON A STRONGER READING THAN THE ONE IT USED. `vreg_reset` enables both rails
#   and then calls the DISABLE path immediately; on an always-on rail that path does not disable but only
#   demotes to LPM - so THE VENDOR'S OWN BRING-UP IS WHAT LEAVES THE RAILS ENABLED AND THE FLAG IS WHAT
#   KEEPS THEM SO. Two consequences, and they are the point: 764 section 3's candidate 1 is WEAKENED, not
#   strengthened - nothing in this tree disables the card's supplies, the vendor's path explicitly enables
#   them, and a board that also boots FROM this eMMC to `fastboot` has had that bus powered and driven; and
#   the candidate stays **UNMEASURED**, which is the honest state, but it is no longer a loose end a reader
#   would expect to be productive. A future reader taking the old sentence at face value could argue FROM
#   it that the card's power is nobody's act - which is the opposite of what the tree says - which is why
#   the sentence is corrected in place above rather than only here.
#
#   AND "THE PMIC IS UNREACHABLE" IS FALSE AS STATED, in a way worth naming. 773 section 3's table counts
#   acts 1/3 as `regulator_*`, hence "no" for reachable from `hc_mem`. That verdict is right about the ACT
#   and wrong about the BLOCK: the PMIC's interface has an MMIO window on this SoC and it is INSIDE A
#   MEGABYTE THIS LADDER ALREADY INSTALLS. `msm8974.dtsi:848-854` - `qcom,spmi@fc4c0000`,
#   `reg = <0xfc4cf000 0x1000>, <0xfc4cb000 0x1000>, <0xfc4ca000 0x1000>` - and `0xFC4` is `ST_GCC_BASE`'s
#   section (`entry_storage.c:280`), with `_gcc_map = 1` in EVERY capture since 694. So the accurate
#   statement is narrower and more interesting: the arbiter's three pages ARE readable from a megabyte the
#   ladder already holds, while THE PMIC'S OWN REGISTERS ARE NOT MEMORY MAPPED AT ALL - they are
#   SPMI-addressed by `usid:offset` - so reading a rail's state would mean driving the arbiter through its
#   command registers, a protocol and not a load. And the path the AP would USE to change a rail is
#   `rpm-smd` (`msm8974.dtsi:2102-2105`, `rpm-channel-name = "rpm_requests"`, `rpm-channel-type = <15>`
#   SMD_APPS_RPM) - a vote into shared memory answered by the RPM firmware, not the arbiter.
#
# NO RUNG IS PROPOSED FROM ANY OF IT: driving an SPMI bus is an act with a failure mode this ladder has not
# measured, the previous candidate in this direction is 748's two dead-end registers, and the ladder has
# never read `0xFC4Cxxxx`. NO set= line follows this block: no arm was built, no park was made, and the

# adds NO device access, NO register, NO window, NO megabyte and NO store.
#
# WHAT THE ARM IS. Four keys, all of them already in a register when the arm runs, and NO new device
# access, no new register, no new window, no new megabyte and no store of any kind:
#   xnu_live_storage_cmd0_cmdlow_seen   the count of the first 1024 samples of CMD0's poll in which
#   xnu_live_storage_cmd1_cmdlow_seen   `PRESENT_STATE 0x24` bit 24 (ST_SDHCI_CMD_LINE_LEVEL, the CMD
#   xnu_live_storage_cid_cmdlow_seen    line's OWN LEVEL) was LOW - one count per command, computed by
#                                       the 724 sampler for EVERY command since rung 24 and published
#                                       by rung 24 for `nidx` alone
#   xnu_live_storage_cid_inhibit_after  the fourth row of 771's table and the only row the log has
#                                       never carried: st_send_command fills it for EVERY command and
#                                       no publish block has ever printed it
#
# WHY IT EXISTS. 771 read the rung-24 press's log as ONE FOUR-ROW TABLE and found the four commands are
# not the same experiment: _cmd0_inhibit_seen = 0x218 beside a command that completed and latched
# INT_RESPONSE; _cmd1_inhibit_seen = 0 and _cid_inhibit_seen = 0 beside 5.09 M polls each with NOTHING
# latched at all; _nidx_inhibit_seen = 0x400 beside a block that armed and FIRED its own response
# timeout at 665.2 us. AND THE ONLY TRACE OF WHAT THE CMD LINE WAS DOING DURING CMD1 OR CMD2 IS ONE
# SAMPLE: `inhibit_last` bit 24 reads LOW for CMD1 and HIGH for CMD2 on every capture in the archive
# (10 cmd0, 8 cmd1, 7 cid). _cmd1_inhibit_last = 0x00F80000 with _cmd1_inhibit_seen = 0 is a
# contradiction the archive already carries, and one sample cannot separate "the block never started
# this command" from "the block drove the line and the inhibit bit is not a reliable witness". The
# count separates them.
#
# CONTAINMENT, MEASURED AND NOT ARGUED. Every new line sits inside `#if STAGE90_XNU_STORAGE_PROBE >= 25`,
# so value 24 is untouched by construction - and that was then MEASURED: the value-24 build from this
# same source came out BYTE-IDENTICAL to the parked armed-storage-f72e9f18 (f72e9f18..., 5552764 bytes,
# exit 0). One press therefore answers the SDC1 pad question AND these four cells, and rung 25's park
# need never be pressed. That is the same relation 767 established between rungs 23 and 24.
#
# WHAT DID NOT MOVE, MEASURED. xnu_arm_entry.bin is 5552764 bytes - the SAME size as the arm before it,
# because the four new keys fitted the padding. 770 measured that an unchanged size is NOT the claim
# that nothing moved, so the claim here rests on the hash (a1378a48..., different) and on the seam
# clause: STAGE90_XNU_SEAM_LR is still 0x8004a2dc and the build accepted it against the linked image,
# so the entry text did NOT cross a page this time. The payload's switch record is BYTE-IDENTICAL to
# rung 23's, rung 24's and rung 25's (6c2b6038..., 682 bytes) - the 763 section 5 trap, checked by cmp
# and not by eye.
#
# WHAT THE PRESS WILL COST AND WHAT IT BUYS. The arm's hazards are rung 25's own - one read of a TLMM
# pad register in a megabyte whose section the arm installs - and its new cells add none. Its answer is
# row 1 of 25's pad table PLUS three counts and one after-bit; neither is a verdict about the card, and
# a zero count is a reading only if the sampler outran the bus, which is why each count is read beside
# its own `_polls`/`_ticks`. NO PRESS IS SPENT HERE AND NONE IS AUTHORIZED: building, parking and
# recording are host-side, and the press is the operator's.

# 773 - THE REACHABLE SET, COUNTED. NO ARM IS BUILT BY THIS STEP AND NOTHING IN `out/` MOVED: the live arm
# is still 772's armed-storage-a1378a48 (STAGE90_XNU_STORAGE_PROBE=25), ARMED AND NOT PRESSED. This block
# exists because the step VERIFIED a load-bearing claim that 769 had only inferred, and because it
# pre-registers the arm that would follow:
#
#   THE CENSUS. 769 section 3 said only the power IRQ's BUS_ON branch applies the SDC1 pads - an inference
#   from reading one function's neighbourhood. It is now counted over the whole vendor tree: every caller
#   of sdhci_msm_setup_pins/setup_pad is sdhci-msm.c:1000 (the dispatcher's only call), :2019 (the BUS_ON
#   branch - the ONLY enable = true), :2034 (power-off, false) and :3144 (teardown, false). And
#   setup_pins carries a latch (:994-995, cfg_sts == enable -> return), so within one Linux boot the pads
#   are written ONCE, on the first BUS_ON - so a board that went straight to fastboot has them at
#   BOOTLOADER state, whatever that is, and nothing in this repository can say what the bootloader wrote.
#
#   THE THREE ACTS, AND THE REACHABLE SET IS SIZE ONE. sdhci-msm.c:2015-2032 does setup_vreg ->
#   setup_pins -> set_vdd_io_vol. Acts 1 and 3 both end in regulator_* (:1826, :1922) - the PMIC, no path
#   from hc_mem - while act 2 lands in MSM_TLMM_BASE + 0x2044 = 0xFD512044, ONE register in the 0xFD5
#   megabyte rung 25 installs. So the vendor's PIN work is the only one of the three a rung can perform,
#   and it is exactly the register rung 26 reads - which is why 769 section 4 could pre-register an
#   expected value at all. AND THE CENSUS RETIRES A STANDING WORRY: setup_vreg's own head says what
#   qcom,vdd-always-on (msm8974-mtp.dtsi:388) means when the data is absent - "vreg info unavailable,
#   assuming the slot is powered by always on domain" (:1835, goto out, ret = 0) - so acts 1 and 3 are
#   satisfied by construction here and their unreachability costs nothing.
#
#   THE RUNG-27 DESIGN, PRE-REGISTERED AND NOT BUILT: read 0xFD512044 (rung 26's own read, kept), compare
#   against ST_TLMM_SDC1_EXPECT = 0x00009F24, and write ONLY if it does not match - one masked RMW over
#   all seven fields at once, then read back. Faithful to msm_tlmm_set_field (gpio-msm-common.c:481-496),
#   which is a plain __raw_readl / mask / __raw_writel / mb() - no unlock, no W1C, no FIFO, no shadow - and
#   a single masked RMW makes the vendor's six-call order IRRELEVANT, which is what makes one store safe
#   where six interleaved ones would need an argument. It STRICTLY CONTAINS rung 26, so one press answers
#   the pad question AND the fix question, and rungs 25 and 26 need never be pressed.
#
#   THE FORK: _pad_raw = 0x00009F24 with _pad_write_skipped = 1 means the pads were already configured and
#   the pad candidate is RETIRED, leaving the PMIC rails (acts 1/3, unreachable) as the whole frontier;
#   anything else with _pad_write_skipped = 0 means the vendor act was never applied and the write has been
#   made and read back. The build clause for rung 27 must assert the store is GUARDED, and the log's safety
#   reading is _pad_writes in {0, 1} as an ACTUAL COUNT and never a constant. A single masked RMW to this
#   register cannot reach another register, another peripheral's pads (0x2044 vs SDC2's 0x2048, disjoint
#   masks), a FUNCTION (there is no function-select field - 769 section 2), the bus (no transfer in
#   flight), or the PMIC/rails/clocks.
#
# NO set= line follows this block: no arm was built, no park was made, and the 35 sets above are unchanged.

# 774 - THE RCG'S ROOT IS ENABLED, AND THE CELL THAT SAYS OTHERWISE READS A BIT NO CODE IN THIS TREE WRITES.
# NO ARM IS BUILT AND NOTHING IN `out/` MOVED: the live arm is still 772's armed-storage-a1378a48
# (STAGE90_XNU_STORAGE_PROBE=25), ARMED AND NOT PRESSED. This block exists because a cell's MEANING was
# wrong in the direction its own name invites, and the correction strengthens a live conclusion:
#
#   WHAT THE TWO CELLS SAY. This ladder publishes xnu_live_storage_clk_rcg_root_en and _rcg_root_status
#   (and the cmd2_ pair), all reading 0, and a reader can take that as "the root clock is off".
#
#   WHICH BIT IS WHICH. clock-local2.c:61-65 defines CMD_RCGR_ROOT_ENABLE_BIT BIT(1) - what you WRITE -
#   and CMD_RCGR_ROOT_STATUS_BIT BIT(31) - what the hardware REPORTS. The vendor reads the STATUS bit in
#   three places, always the same way (:299 _rcg_clk_handoff, :727 and :804): if the bit is SET it returns
#   HANDOFF_DISABLED_CLK, else HANDOFF_ENABLED_CLK. So SET means DISABLED and CLEAR means ENABLED, and
#   _rcg_root_status = 0 is therefore a POSITIVE reading that the SDC1 apps root is enabled, by the
#   vendor's own test.
#
#   AND _rcg_root_en READS A BIT NOTHING WRITES. grep -rn 'ROOT_ENABLE' arch/arm/mach-msm/ drivers/clk/
#   returns ONE hit - the #define. rcg_clk_prepare (:152-161) is a no-op that only WARNs if the rate was
#   never set; __clk_pre_reparent (clock.c:247) recurses into the parent's prepare/enable, which for an
#   rcg is that same no-op; and the one path that DOES write CMD_RCGR does not write that bit - set_rate_mnd
#   (:127-150) writes M_REG/N_REG/D_REG, then CFG_RCGR's DIV_MASK/SRC_SEL_MASK/MND_MODE_MASK, then
#   rcg_update_config: five words and the update bit, never the root enable. So its 0 carries no
#   information about whether the root is running. That is m737's shape and m776's shape again: a cell
#   whose NAME states a direction, read as though the 0 were the finding, when the finding is the
#   neighbouring cell and its sign is the opposite of the one the name invites.
#
#   WHAT IT CHANGES. It STRENGTHENS 771 section 7 - the clock is not a candidate - with a second,
#   independent reading that shares no mechanism with the divider arithmetic (384 MHz / 960 = 400,000 Hz
#   exactly). It disturbs no other rung: nothing in the press path reads _rcg_root_en as evidence of a
#   disabled clock, and rung_para 5's sentence is not made false. It does NOT say the clock reaches the
#   PADS - rung 5 already separated a branch's REQUEST (CBCR bit 0) from the framework's belief (bit 31),
#   and this closes the ROOT half while leaving the PAD half where rung 25 put it.
#
# NO set= line follows this block: no arm was built, no park was made, and the 35 sets above are unchanged.

# 776: THE RUNG-28 ARM - armed-storage-d5d98738, STAGE90_XNU_STORAGE_PROBE=27.
# Built, parked and recorded here. HOST-SIDE ONLY: no device action, no press, no gate
# against a device, no runner, no firer. Rungs 27, 26, 25 and 23's parks are all intact;
# this arm SUPERSEDES rung 27 because it strictly contains it, MEASURED rather than argued
# (the value-26 build from this same source is byte-identical to 8096cb2c).
#
# WHAT IT IS. The FIRST STORE THIS LADDER HAS EVER MADE TO A SECOND DEVICE: st_pad_census -
# the body rung 25 added to READ the TLMM's SDC1 pad-control register at physical 0xFD512044
# - now ends in an `if`. When the 32-bit read already equals ST_TLMM_SDC1_EXPECT (0x00009F24,
# the value this board's own qcom,pad-pull-on / qcom,pad-drv-on arrays produce through the
# kernel's own shift and mask) it publishes _pad_write_skipped = 1 and _pad_writes = 0 and
# NO STORE IS MADE AT ALL. Otherwise it writes (raw & ~MASK) | EXPECT - ONE masked
# read-modify-write over the UNION OF THE SEVEN FIELDS, 0x0001FFFF: hdrive clk/cmd/data at
# bits 6/3/0 and pull clk/cmd/data/rclk at 13/11/9/15 - and publishes _pad_write_skipped = 0,
# _pad_writes = 1, _pad_wrote, _pad_after and _pad_after_match.
#   xnu_live_storage_pad_write_skipped / _writes / _wrote / _after / _after_match
#
# THE BITS OUTSIDE THE SEVEN ARE THE BITS THE READ HANDED BACK, carried through unchanged -
# which is what makes this a field write and not a whole-word write to a register a
# bootloader may have owned. And the value written is the VENDOR'S OWN: sdhci_msm_setup_pad
# (sdhci-msm.c:964) walks those same seven fields to those same two arrays, so the guard is
# what makes the ANSWER readable and NOT what makes the store safe - even an unguarded fire
# would be a word Linux itself stores at every CORE_PWRCTL_BUS_ON (sdhci-msm.c:2015-2032).
#
# THE STORE IS A PLAIN READ-MODIFY-WRITE WITH A MASK, field for field msm_tlmm_set_field's
# (gpio-msm-common.c:481-496): no unlock sequence, no write-one-to-clear, no FIFO, no shadow
# register - so one masked RMW over the union makes the vendor's six-call ORDER irrelevant,
# and that is why one store is safe here where six interleaved ones would need an argument.
#
# AND THE BUILD REFUSES THE ARM WITHOUT THE GUARD, TWICE AND INDEPENDENTLY. The store COUNT
# is 0 at values 24..26 and exactly 1 at 27, one clause read against the rung rather than two
# policies; the one `str` must be PREDICATED or SPANNED BY A CONDITIONAL BRANCH in the body's

# HAS BEEN MADE, with _pad_after = 0x00009F24 meaning it landed.

# so 0 and 1 are the only two values a well-formed run can carry.
#

#   xnu_live_storage_cmd1_status_any = 0x00000000 over _cmd1_polls = 0x004da000 = 5,087,232

#   7062, which is 778's own class: 0x004DA000 is 5,087,232 and this file already carried the
#   correct pair at its line 5349. The 1,024 difference is the poll loop's own bound and not a
#   reading of this press's)
#   xnu_live_storage_cmd1_timeout    = 1
# is a reading under a ONE-BIT-plus-ERR mask and NOT under the widened word - the same masked
# reading rung 28 would have produced. The source says it in its own words and always did: the
# `>= 14` window's comment reads "the interval it was open for is exactly CMD0's own send and
# poll, and there is no path out of st_cmd_path that reaches the gate, CMD1, or a return with the
# enable still set". **783 read the SCOPE by counting which COMMAND each FUNCTION carries; a
# window is an INTERVAL, and the two are not the same question.** The false sentence is now in
# five places - the entry source's `>= 28` comment (src/entry/entry_storage.c, the RUNG 29 block
# at the `st_cmd_path` window), this file's `# 785:` block, tools/verify_press_ready.sh's value-28
# narration and its rung_para 28 paragraph, the 785 experiment doc and the 785 commit message.
# Corrected in place in this file and in tools/verify_press_ready.sh; the ENTRY SOURCE comment is
# COST-owed to the next build, because correcting a comment forces one (771's rule) and this arm
# is already spent.
#
# 4. AND IT NARROWS 765's PREMISE, WHICH IS THE SHARPER OF THE TWO FINDINGS. 765 established that
# INT_STATUS here is a GATED VIEW and every arm since has read `_status_any = 0` as a reading
# about a one-bit MASK. But `SDHCI_INT_ERROR` (bit 15, 0x8000) IS ENABLED ON EVERY ARM - item 1's
# `_ena_wrote_back`/`_ena_readback` pair is the measurement - and on this block INT_ERR TRACKS THE
# ERROR BITS rather than standing beside them:
#   `_nidx_status_any = 0x00018000` = ERR | TIMEOUT   (CMD3's TIMEOUT, rung 23's cell reproduced)
#   `_cid_status_any  = 0x00028000` = ERR | CRC       (item 2)
# So a zero `_status_any` on the narrow arms was NOT blind to the EXISTENCE of an error. What a
# one-bit command window could not show is the error's IDENTITY, and what it could not show at all
# is a non-error bit other than the completion. **765's premise is true and NARROWER than the
# ladder has been stating it: the widening buys identity, not existence - which is exactly what
# item 2 shows, and why the CMD2 row changes from 0 to a named CRC while the CMD1 row would not
# have changed at all.**
#
# 5. RUNG 28's PAD QUESTION IS ANSWERED, IN THE SAME PRESS, OFF 785's CONTAINMENT CLAIM - AND THE
# ANSWER IS THE ROW NOTHING IS WRITTEN ON.
#   xnu_live_storage_pad_raw          = 0x00009f24   (== _pad_expect: the register ALREADY held it)
#   xnu_live_storage_pad_match        = 1
#   xnu_live_storage_pad_write_skipped= 1
#   xnu_live_storage_pad_writes       = 0            (NOTHING WAS STORED)
#   xnu_live_storage_pad_cmd_pull     = 3, _pad_data_pull = 3, _pad_rclk_pull = 1,
#   xnu_live_storage_pad_clk_hdrv     = 4, _pad_cmd_hdrv = 4, _pad_data_hdrv = 4
# So the TLMM's SDC1 pad register was ALREADY at the vendor's CORE_PWRCTL_BUS_ON state when the
# arm read it - the bootloader put it there, since no rung and no Linux on this path wrote it -
# and 768 section 5's other half is RETIRED, with `PULL SDC1_CMD` present as 769 section 2's
# mechanism requires. **The guard held: the arm's first row is the one on which its ONE STORE does
# not happen, and `_pad_writes = 0` is that fact read out of the log.** 776 section 3's `0x9E00`
# row (pulls present, drive off) did not occur and the two-row fork's else arm is not the row this
# device is on.
#
# 6. THE CMD LINE MOVED DURING THREE OF THE FOUR COMMANDS, WHICH RETIRES A CANDIDATE.
#   _cmd0_cmdlow_seen = 0x1bc (444 of the first 1024 samples)  _cmd0_polls = 0x219
#   _cmd1_cmdlow_seen = 0x28a (650 of 1024)                    _cmd1_polls = 0x004da000
#   _nidx_cmdlow_seen = 0x176 (374 of 1024)                    _nidx_polls = 0x000005d5
#   _cid_cmdlow_seen  = 0x0 - and its window was ONE poll (_cid_polls = 1), so it is a window too
#   short to sample the line and NOT a reading that the line was still.
# 764 section 4's candidate 3 ("nothing was ever driven onto the bus") is therefore RETIRED: the
# block drives the line. What stays open is what the line was driven WITH and what the card did
# about it.
#
# 7. WHAT THIS PRESS DOES NOT DECIDE, NAMED RATHER THAN LEFT. The CRC is a COMMAND-LEVEL error
# bit and the block raises it AT THE FIRST POLL after the command word was written; rung 6 set the
# card clock to 400 kHz, at which a 48-bit command and its response take ~240 us, so the window
# CMD2's own cells describe (`_cid_ticks = 0x11`) is far too short for a card's answer to have been
# clocked in. `_cid_stale = 1` with `_cid_clear_after = 0` says the latch was CLEAN before the
# command, so the bit did not stand there from an earlier window - but whether it is (a) the card
# answering and the block refusing the answer, (b) the block signalling an ILLEGAL COMMAND because
# CMD1's 1.2 s timeout left its command state machine wedged (rung 19 measured exactly that
# wedge), or (c) the bit re-asserting from the pad the arm did not write, is NOT decided by this
# press. `_nidx_status_pre = 0x00028000` - the same two bits still set at CMD3's window, one
# window later - is the cell that says the pair is STICKY across at least one further command, and
# it is the cheapest next reading there is: it is already in this capture.
#
# NOTHING HERE IS A NEW ARM, A NEW FILE IN out/, OR A DEVICE ACTION: out/ is byte-identical
# before and after this block. THE GOAL IS STILL NOT MET - the block names an error on CMD2 and
# still completes no transfer, no filesystem is reached and no mount is made, so
# TWRP-to-storage stays withheld.

# 787: THE RUNG-30 ARM - armed-storage-dfc4ae78, STAGE90_XNU_STORAGE_PROBE=29.
# Built, parked and recorded here. Rung 29's park (armed-storage-5fca6210) is intact and is SPENT;
# every park before it is intact. This arm SUPERSEDES rung 29 because it strictly contains it,
# MEASURED rather than argued (the value-28 build from this same source is byte-identical to the
# parked rung-29 arm and to its own xnu_arm_entry.bin - see the containment paragraph). NO PRESS IS
# SPENT AND NONE IS AUTHORIZED: the press is the operator's, and the path to it is the two commands
# readiness prints, run by hand once each.
#
# WHAT IT IS. 786 read rung 29's press and found, out of the capture's own line order, that rung
# 14's restore - `_ena_wrote_back = 0x00000000` at capture line 8789 - runs BEFORE the
# between-commands gate and therefore before CMD1. So `st_cmd_path`'s widened window covers CMD0
# alone, and CMD1 has run with the completion bit NOT enabled on every arm from rung 14 on:
#
#   _cmd1_status_any = 0x00000000   over   _cmd1_polls = 0x004da000 = 5,087,232
#   _cmd1_timeout    = 0x00000001   and    _cmd1_complete = 0x00000000
#
# CMD1 is SEND_OP_COND - the command an eMMC must answer for this ladder to move at all, and the
# question 764 section 5 left open. So this arm is the first time the ladder gives that command an
# enable that can report anything.
#
# THE ACT IS TWO MORE STORES TO THE SAME INT_ENABLE 0x34, IN AN INTERVAL THE LADDER HAS BEEN
# RUNNING CMD1 IN ALL ALONG. Same register, same constant (ST_SDHCI_INT_ENABLE_CMD == 0x000F0001 -
# rung 23's five bits: RESPONSE | TIMEOUT | CRC | END_BIT | INDEX, and NOT the vendor's eleven),
# same width, no new address, no new megabyte, no new device. SIGNAL_ENABLE 0x38 is still READ and
# never written, so nothing here can raise a line this image cannot service. The window's two ends
# are bodies of their own - st_cmd1_enable_open (:2976, called once at :4526) and st_cmd1_enable_restore (:2999, called once at :4582) - called
# once each from st_cmd_path, which is what keeps that function's OWN device surface at rung 14's
# and keeps every rung-14 clause in build_entry.sh true at the digit rather than relaxed. The value
# it puts back is the word the open RETURNED, so `_c1_ena_wrote == _c1_ena_wrote_back` is a READING
# and not two evaluations of one expression.
#
# NO NEW KEY AND NO NEW STATUS CELL. The two bodies publish only the four words that make the
# window itself readable - _c1_ena_wrote, _c1_ena_held, _c1_ena_wrote_back, _c1_ena_readback - and
# NEITHER BODY TOUCHES INT_STATUS 0x30: each is one store to INT_ENABLE 0x34 and its readback, which
# is the same one-register surface rung 14's own restore has. So what this arm changes is what the
# CMD1 cells the ladder ALREADY CARRIES can mean - _cmd1_status_any, _cmd1_err, _cmd1_complete,
# _cmd1_timeout, and _cmd1_stale / _cmd1_status_after, which are st_send_command's own entrance and
# exit reads of 0x30 and are published for every command - and not a new reading beside them. That
# is rung 23's shape one command over: the widening changed what CMD3's existing cells could mean.
# NO NEW REGISTER, NO NEW WIDTH, NO NEW WINDOW IN ANY OTHER FUNCTION, NO NEW MEGABYTE, NO NEW
# DEVICE, NO NEW COMMAND.
#
# THE ANSWER SPACE, FOUR ROWS, AND THE FIRST IS THE ONE THAT MOVES THE LADDER. With the five bits
# standing across CMD1's send and its poll:
#   * bit 0 (SDHCI_INT_RESPONSE) VISIBLE means CMD1 COMPLETED and the block latched it. The latch is
#     a hardware event the enable only GATES THE VIEW OF, so on that row the 1.2 s "timeout" every
#     arm from rung 14 on has reported was THIS LADDER'S OWN MASK and the completion may have been
#     there all along. That row changes what the next arm is: the ladder stops asking what is wrong
#     with the card and starts reading CMD1's own answer.
#   * ERR | TIMEOUT (0x00018000) means the block armed its OWN response timeout and the card did not
#     answer within it - the reading CMD3 already carries (_nidx_status_any = 0x00018000 beside
#     _nidx_status_pre = 0x00028000) - and puts the subject on the card and on the power/clock path
#     784 gave a shape to.
#   * CRC, END_BIT or INDEX means the card answered and the answer was malformed.
#   * NOTHING AT ALL with all five bits enabled is the strong negative: the block set no bit of
#     INT_STATUS during a command it was given.
#
# **AND THE ERR | TIMEOUT ROW IS NOT ALREADY EXCLUDED, WHICH IS THIS ARM'S SECOND QUESTION.** 786
# section 4 read the CMD2 and CMD3 rows (ERR | CRC, ERR | TIMEOUT) as showing that bit 15 TRACKS the
# error bits, and concluded that CMD1's row "would not have moved at all". But _ena_readback =
# 0x00008000 in rung 29's OWN capture says bit 15 STANDS during CMD1 - no write clears it - and BOTH
# of 786's rows come from arms on which the specific error bit was ENABLED. Two readings are open
# and this window separates them:
#   (a) bit 15 rises with any error whatever its own bit's enable - then no error occurred at CMD1
#       and only bit 0 can be new;
#   (b) bit 15 rises only when the specific error bit is enabled - then CMD1 may have timed out
#       INVISIBLY on every arm from rung 14 on, and 786 section 4's sentence is too strong.
#
# A NEGATIVE IS READ ONLY WHERE THE LINE MOVED (771's rule, one window over): _cmd1_cmdlow_seen on
# rung 29's capture is 0x0000028a = 650 of the first 1024 samples, so the CMD line DID move during
# CMD1 on that arm, and a zero status count beside it is a statement about the block and not about
# a bus nobody drove. _cmd1_polls and _cmd1_ticks are read BESIDE it, because a sampler slower than
# one bit period could miss a transmission and report a zero.
#
# NO CELL OF THIS ARM IS READ AS AN ANSWER FROM THE CARD. 0x40ff8080 stands in the RESPONSE
# registers after a command that TIMED OUT (_nidx_resp_pre = 0x00000000 then _nidx_resp_post =
# 0x40ff8080 beside _nidx_status_any = 0x00018000), the image never WRITES those registers (every
# one of its accesses to RESPONSE 0x10 is a read), and rung 19's capture records the same word
# BEFORE CMD3 was put on the bus. So a non-zero _cmd1_resp is NOT evidence the card answered. The
# comment at the head of CMD1 says of exactly this value "the card ANSWERED"; that inference is
# unsupported and is COST-owed to this arm's successor.
#
# AND THE CLAUSE IS THE READING, NOT THIS SENTENCE. build_entry.sh's `xnu_entry_787` asserts, against
# the LINKED image, for each of the two new bodies: its device set is exactly [f9824934:ldr
# f9824934:str], its image side is EMPTY, it is referenced exactly once from st_cmd_path, the OPEN's
# call falls BEFORE the second st_send_command and the CLOSE's AFTER it. The last two are the
# property 785's false sentence needed and are positions read out of the linked image, not out of a
# comment.

# 788: THE FOUR-ARM ENABLE MATRIX - HOST-SIDE ONLY, A READING OF CAPTURES ALREADY ON DISK.

# INT_STATUS read ZERO for the whole window - _status_any is st_send_command's own field, the FIRST
# non-zero INT_STATUS of any kind read RAW with no mask (src/entry/entry_storage.c:2635-2637):

#     rung29-2win   v28   _cid_polls = 1           _cid_status_any = 0x00028000   _cid_err = 0x00020000
#   CMD3 (st_cmd3_noidx), enable written 0x00000001, held 0x00008001:

#
# 30,537,728 READS OF INT_STATUS, WITH SDHCI_INT_ERROR STANDING IN INT_ENABLE THE WHOLE TIME, AND
# BIT 15 APPEARED IN NONE OF THEM. The two arms whose enable ALSO carried the specific bits reported
# ERR | CRC and ERR | TIMEOUT AT THE FIRST POLL. So a standing bit 15 in INT_ENABLE is NOT
# sufficient for bit 15 to appear in INT_STATUS on this block, and 786 section 4's sentence - that
# bit 15 TRACKS the error bits so a zero _status_any on a narrow arm was never blind to an error's
# EXISTENCE - is refuted by the archive's own data: its two rows were both taken on arms whose
# enable carried the bit, which cannot distinguish TRACKING from CO-LATCHING.
#
# AND 786 SECTION 4's CONCLUSION `the widening buys identity, not existence` IS WITHDRAWN AS
# STATED. At these two windows the widening is what makes an error appear AT ALL.
#

# 791: THE CMD2 CENSUS - THE IMMEDIATE CRC IS UNIQUE TO THE ONE COMMAND THAT ASKS FOR A 136-BIT
# RESPONSE, AND THE NARROW ARMS' ZERO IS A MASKED READING, MEASURED.
# HOST-SIDE ONLY. NOTHING WAS BUILT, NO SOURCE WAS EDITED AND out/ IS BYTE-IDENTICAL BEFORE AND AFTER
# THIS BLOCK, so the spent rung-30 arm's park (armed-storage-dfc4ae78, 11 members) and every park
# before it are unchanged and every set= line in this file still resolves. NO PRESS IS SPENT, NO ARM
# IS ARMED AND NONE IS AUTHORIZED.
#
# THE CENSUS. Nine arms carry CMD2's cells and EXACTLY THE TWO WHOSE CMD2 WINDOW CARRIED THE CRC
# ENABLE READ NON-ZERO:
#   rung 29 / rung 30   INT_ENABLE 0x000f0001   _cid_status_any = 0x00028000   at _cid_any_polls = 0x1
#   rungs 17/18/19/20/21/22/24   INT_ENABLE 0x00000001   _cid_status_any = 0x00000000   over ~5.09M polls
# 0x00028000 is SDHCI_INT_ERR (bit 15) | SDHCI_INT_CRC (bit 17).
#
# THE BRACKET, AND IT LEAVES NOTHING BETWEEN THE CLEAN READ AND THE LATCH:
#   _cid_stale       = 0x00000001   INT_STATUS at CMD2's entrance, AFTER its own 0x34 store: bit 0 only
#   _cid_clear_wrote = 0x00000001   the write-1-to-clear
#   _cid_clear_after = 0x00000000   THE LATCH WAS CLEAN
#   _cid_word = _cid_word_read = 0x00000209   the block accepted the word into its COMMAND register
#   _cid_status_any = 0x00028000 at _cid_any_polls = 0x00000001
# The only device accesses between _cid_clear_after and that first poll are the ARGUMENT store, the
# COMMAND store, and the COMMAND and PRESENT_STATE readbacks. So the block latched ERR|CRC between
# being handed the command word and the next read of INT_STATUS.
#
# AND IT IS FAR TOO EARLY FOR A RESPONSE, SAID WITHOUT ANY CLOCK FREQUENCY. _cmd0_ticks - the same
# counter, boot and bus, for one 48-bit no-response frame - is 0x132d/0x132a/0x1325/0x132d/0x1328/
# 0x1327/0x132a = 4909/4906/4901/4909/4904/4903/4906 across SEVEN arms (spread 8 ticks, 0.16 per cent).
# _cid_ticks = 0x00000011 = 17 IS 0.35 PER CENT OF ONE SUCH FRAME - before a start bit, a command index
# and a CRC could have been shifted out, let alone a 136-bit response shifted in. The narrow arms' CMD2
# poll ran _cid_ticks = 0x015f9xxx = about 23,040,000 ticks, roughly 4700 _cmd0 frames, and read zero
# at every one of them.
#
# THE ISOLATION: THE CORRELATE IS THE RESPONSE LENGTH AND NOT THE CRC ENABLE. Three commands have now
# been given a wide enough enable, and the command word is a property of the COMMAND and not of the
# enable:
#   CMD1  SEND_OP_COND       PRESENT        0x0102   48-bit   CRC check OFF   COMPLETED, poll 1236, no error bit
#   CMD3  SET_RELATIVE_ADDR  R1_NOIDX       0x030a   48-bit   CRC check ON    ERR|TIMEOUT, BIT 17 NEVER SET
#   CMD2  ALL_SEND_CID       R2             0x0209   136-bit  CRC check ON    ERR|CRC at poll 1, 17 ticks
# CMD3's word carries the SAME 0x08 CRC bit as CMD2's, so the CRC bit's presence is not explained by the
# command's own CRC check; the one thing CMD2 has that no other command in this ladder has is a 136-BIT
# RESPONSE REQUEST. The table's missing corner is 136-bit with the CRC check OFF - ONE BIT.
#
# AND THE NARROW ARMS' ZERO IS A MASKED READING, MEASURED RATHER THAN INFERRED. Rung 24 is the one
# narrow arm whose NEXT body opens a WIDE window, and that makes it the control the census otherwise
# lacks:
#   _cid_ena_wrote   = 0x00000001   one bit, no CRC
#   _cid_status_any  = 0x00000000   over _cid_polls = 0x004db000 = 5091328 reads
#   _cid_status_post = 0x00000000   read with INT_ENABLE restored to 0
#   _nidx_status_pre = 0x00018000   THE NEXT BODY, under the FIVE-BIT word
# ERR|TIMEOUT was sitting in the latch at the top of the next body, one command after a window whose
# poll had read zero 5,091,328 times. So at CMD2 (1) 788 section 3's conclusion is now a MEASUREMENT AT
# THIS WINDOW rather than an inference from other windows, and (2) _cid_status_post = 0 DOES NOT MEAN
# THE LATCH IS CLEAN, because it is read through INT_ENABLE = 0.
#
# AND THAT SECOND POINT IS A NAMED DEFECT CLASS, NOT ONE CELL. Every *_wrote_back cell in the archive
# is 0x00000000 - every window in this ladder closes by storing int_enable, which is zero - so ALL FOUR
# *_status_post CELLS ARE 100 PER CENT MASKED READS:
#   _ena_status_post (14 onward) / _cid_status_post (16 onward) / _nidx_status_post (20 onward) /
#   _rca_status_post (18/19) - every one of them 0x00000000 on every arm.
# The _*_readback = 0x00008000 beside them is the tell that the store happened at all (bit 15 stands in
# INT_ENABLE and no write clears it) and is not itself a status reading.
#
# WHAT IT DOES NOT SEPARATE, NAMED AND NOT LEFT. On the narrow control the latched value has bit 16 and
# NOT bit 17 while the command word is IDENTICAL, so two mechanisms are admissible: (i) the enable
# switches the CHECK on, so no CRC check runs without the CRC enable and rung 24's condition was the
# block's own response timeout; or (ii) the enable gates VISIBILITY only and the CRC bit is an EARLY
# SPURIOUS LATCH raised when a CRC check is enabled on a 136-bit request. And a third asymmetry a
# reader must not read past: because the wide arms BREAK AT POLL 1, the ladder has NEVER observed
# whether a wide enable at CMD2 later latches TIMEOUT as well - the wide reading is a FIRST latch and
# the narrow reading is a LATER one, and whether they are one condition seen twice or two conditions is
# not in the archive.
#
# THE PRE-REGISTERED NEXT ARM IS ONE BIT OUT OF CMD2'S FLAGS, AND ITS BEST ROW REACHES THE CID. CMD2
# (ALL_SEND_CID, opcode 2, argument 0) sent with MMC_RSP_PRESENT | MMC_RSP_136 - the CRC flag dropped
# and NOTHING ELSE MOVED: same opcode, same argument, same window, same position in the driver's order,
# same five-bit INT_ENABLE. Flags 0x07 -> PRESENT|136, word 0x0209 -> 0x0201. Dropping the CRC check
# from a 136-bit response is legal on the wire: the card still returns the CID and the block simply does
# not check it. FOUR ROWS:
#   _cid_complete = 1          THE CID IS TAKEN - the largest single step available from here, after
#                              which the driver order is CMD9 (CSD), CMD7 (select), CMD16, then data.
#   ERR|TIMEOUT (0x00018000)   the CRC latch needs the command's own CRC flag, and the real condition
#                              at CMD2 is the block's own response timeout - which moves the subject to
#                              why a 136-bit response never arrives.
#   ERR|CRC (0x00028000) anyway  the CRC bit is not about the command's CRC flag at all, WHICH REFUTES
#                              the isolation above and puts the 136-bit path itself on the block.
#   nothing, full bound, and the next wide read shows TIMEOUT   the same as row 2 from the other side,
#                              and it separates (i) from (ii) by whether the bit appears at all.
# The control is in the same log: _cmd0_ticks and CMD1's own completion bracket the new word from both
# ends. THE ARM IS PRE-REGISTERED AND NOT BUILT - building it moves out/, and a build is a later step's
# act, not this one's.
#
# WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO. It builds nothing and spends no press; out/ is byte-identical and every park is
# intact. It does not decide (i) versus (ii), and it does not say whether CMD2's condition is on the card
# or on the block - it isolates the CORRELATE and does not name the cause. And IT DOES NOT REACH THE
# GOAL: no transfer completes, no filesystem is reached and no mount is made, so TWRP-TO-STORAGE STAYS
# WITHHELD.

# OWED: the pre-registered one-bit arm above (built by a later step, pressed only by the operator); the

# 793: THE 136-BIT READ HAS BEEN TAKEN NINE TIMES AND NEVER ONCE HELD A CID, AND 792's ROW 1 IS AN
# OVERCLAIM CORRECTED BEFORE THE PRESS.
#
# HOST-SIDE ONLY. No device action, no press, no gate against a device, no runner, no firer, NOTHING
# BUILT. `out/` is byte-identical to what 792 left it: the armed arm `armed-storage-f9613649` is
# UNSPENT and its eleven-member park is intact, and no source under `src/` was edited. ONE PRESS SPENT:
# NONE. NO PRESS IS AUTHORIZED.

# WHY THIS BLOCK EXISTS. 792 section 7 pre-registered rung 31's four rows and gave the first as
# "`_cid_complete = 1` - THE CID IS TAKEN", and the same sentence is carried into
# `tools/verify_press_ready.sh`, the two places whose text the next press PRINTS. The claim rests on an
# assumption that was never checked: that the four RESPONSE words read after CMD2 would be A CID if the
# command completed. The archive refutes it, nine times over.
#
# (1) THE FOUR WORDS ARE READ UNCONDITIONALLY. `st_all_send_cid`'s tail (`src/entry/entry_storage.c`,
#     the block citing `sdhci.c:1163-1172`, the driver's own 136-bit branch, word 3 first) reads
#     RESPONSE +12/+8/+4/+0 and publishes `_cid_raw0..3` and `_cid_resp0..3`. There is NO `if` in that
#     block, so the cells fire on EVERY arm whatever the command did. Their CONTENT is a separate
#     question from `_cid_complete`.

# (2) NINE ARMS CARRY THEM AND ALL NINE ARE BYTE-FOR-BYTE IDENTICAL. rungs 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 24,
#     29 and 30 - seven narrow windows and two wide enough to report an error, two of them having
#     latched `ERR | CRC` at poll 1 - hold
#         `_cid_raw0..3`  = 0x0040ff80 / 0x80000000 / 0 / 0
#         `_cid_resp0..3` = 0x40ff8080 / 0 / 0 / 0
#     and the eight published words do not vary on any of them. A CID is 128 bits; three of four words
#     zero is not a CID. THE LADDER HAS NEVER READ A CID - and completing the command is not by itself
#     what would give it one, because these cells were read on nine arms that did NOT complete and read
#     the same thing.

# (3) AND THE WORD IS NOT A DEFAULT - THE BLOCK MOVES, AND THE LOG'S OWN LINE ORDER PROVES IT.
#     `st_resp_before` reads the SAME four offsets in the SAME `<< 8` arithmetic (deliberately, since

#         8777: `_cmd0_resp      = 0`            (RESPONSE+0, after CMD0)

#     Rungs 18 and 29 are in the same order. THE REGISTER WAS ZERO WHEN THE LADDER ARRIVED, so
#     everything it later holds the block put there itself. It does NOT say which command moved it -
#     two commands, one interval, and no cell separates them.

#
#   1a - `_cid_complete = 1` AND the register block CHANGED: `_cid_resp0` off `0x40ff8080`, or any of

#        CMD7 (select), CMD16 (block length), then data.

#        on this ladder under suspicion - 790 section 1's CMD1 row and its 2.094 ratio included.
#

# and row 3 is SHARPENED: `_cid_raw2`/`_cid_raw3` zero on the two wide arms is a second,

# "`_cid_complete = 1` - THE CID IS TAKEN. The driver order opens: CMD9 (CSD), CMD7 (select), CMD16

# THIS IMAGE.
#
# (1) THE VOCABULARY IS FOUR OPCODES. `grep -cE '^#define ST_CMD_OP_' src/entry/entry_storage.c` = 4,
#     and they are opcodes 0, 1, 2 and 3: CMD0, CMD1, CMD2, CMD3. There is NO `ST_CMD_OP_SEND_CSD`
#     define at all, no body, and no call site.

#     1) and the only thing after it in `entry_storage_probe` (`:5144`) is `st_pwr_irq_after()` and
#     then a return. Inside, the sequence is CMD0 (`:4506`), CMD1 (`:4603`), CMD2 (`:4678`/`:4680`),
#     CMD3 (`:4742`/`:4775`).

# (3) AND THERE IS NO DATA PATH - measured, anchored, case-SENSITIVE:
#         grep -rnE '\b(BLOCK_SIZE|BLOCK_COUNT|TRANSFER_MODE|ADMA|SDHCI_DATA|SDHCI_BLOCK|DMA_ADDRESS)\b' \
#              src/ --include=*.c --include=*.h
#     returns TWO lines and BOTH ARE COMMENTS - one of them the source's own "no data-path register at
#     all" (`:2076`). `ST_SDHCI_DMA_ADDRESS 0x00` is defined and READ TWICE AS A VERSION/IDENTITY WORD
#     (`:695`, `:4932`), never as a transfer address. The NAME is in the tree; the PATH is not.
#
# WHAT THIS CHANGES. A perfect CID at rung 31 does NOT move this ladder one command closer to
# 「挂载存储」. The ladder's frontier is TWO frontiers and only one had been named: (i) the CMD2 bit the
# last five steps have been on, and (ii) THE BREADTH GAP - the storage path is an INITIALIZATION
# SEQUENCE that stops after CMD3, and a mount needs CMD9, CMD7, CMD16 and a data path behind them.
# Row 1a is STILL WORTH THE PRESS: it is the last item this sequence asks for and it settles the 136-bit
# question. What changes is what row 1a BUYS.

# WHERE IT LANDED. `docs/experiments/**` is a historical record and is NOT rewritten, so 792's and 793's

# LANE-ownerless case and NOT the COST case, THE SECOND TIME IN TWO STEPS the same file had no live
# owner to report a wrong press-facing sentence to.

# AND A DEFECT THIS STEP MADE ITSELF, recorded because the selector is the lesson. The first pass of
# that search was `-i` and UNANCHORED and returned fifteen lines - FOURTEEN OF THEM `deadman`
# (`stage90_disarm_deADMAn_timer`, `stage90_arm_deADMAn_reset`, `g_deADMAn_armed`). The selector
# matched a substring of a word it was never about, and a table built from that output would have said

# COST. None to the armed arm: no source was edited and `out/` did not move. The next BUILD's subject is

# 795: THE RUNG-31 PRESS - THE IMMEDIATE CRC NEEDED THE FLAG AS WELL AS THE 136-BIT REQUEST, AND WHAT
# REPLACED IT IS THE BLOCK'S OWN 665.2 us TIMEOUT, WHICH IS AN UNSET REGISTER.
#
# ONE PRESS SPENT, AND IT WAS AUTHORIZED BY THE OPERATOR BEFORE THE GATE WAS RUN. One gate (exit 0, 607
# lines), one runner (EXIT 0), one `fastboot boot`, nothing flashed, nothing written to storage, no
# reboot. `out/` moved: the arm in it is rung 31's and it is now SPENT. `4a2fe00b` present as 'device';
# `33e80afe` ABSENT from both `adb devices` and `fastboot devices` at fire time. Fired 2026-09-28
# 03:43:44 UTC. Capture `out/stage90/captures/rung31-nocrc-20260928-034344-last_kmsg.txt` 633,586 B
# sha256 `9c0baf80380f33ad67d00dbf73c7c59e647d4afe59ec238a2d192186e8989f8b`, archived by hand with its
# gate.log and run.log (the runner does NOT archive). The runner's verdict is 7 PASS / 1 FAIL / 3 UNREAD
# COUNTED PER CRITERION - eleven criteria, printed twice in one log (m751) - and it is identical to
# rungs 29's and 30's, so this press added no failure.
#
# THE ARM TOOK EFFECT. `_cid_flags = 0x00000003`; `_cid_word = _cid_word_read = 0x00000201` - the
# block's own copy of `COMMAND 0x0E`; `_cid_op = 2`.
#
# THE HEADLINE: ROW 2 LANDED. The latch moved `ERR | CRC` (`0x00028000`) at poll 1 in 17 ticks to
# `ERR | TIMEOUT` (`0x00018000`) at poll 1,797 (= `0x00000705`) in 12,770 ticks (= `0x000031e2`) - a
# 751x longer windup - with `_cid_err` `0x00020000` -> `0x00010000` and `_cid_complete = 0`. SO THE
# IMMEDIATE CRC NEEDS BOTH CONJUNCTS: a 136-bit request AND the CRC check in the command word. 791
# section 4 named the length and missed that the flag is necessary - CMD3 carries the flag and never
# latched bit 17, and this arm does not either.
#
# AND THE 136-BIT COMMAND WAS ACTUALLY DRIVEN THIS TIME. `_cid_cmdlow_seen` moved 0 -> 445 of 1024
# (`0x1bd`); on rung 30 it was 0, because the immediate CRC landed BEFORE the command went on the wire.
# `_cid_inhibit_after` moved 1 -> 0, so CMD2 no longer wedged the block, so CMD3 WAS SENT
# (`_nidx_sent = 0x1`) for the first time since rung 19.
#
# 12,770 TICKS IS 665.2 us, AND IT IS A CONSTANT. CMD3 in the same boot: `_nidx_polls = 0x701` = 1,793,
# `_nidx_ticks = 0x31e4` = 12,772 = 665.3 us, `_nidx_status_any = 0x00018000`, `_nidx_err = 0x00010000`,
# `_nidx_cmdlow_seen = 0x187` = 391 of 1024 - the same bound to within 0.02 per cent, and the same bound
# rung 24 measured (768's block: "a break at poll 1789 in 665.2 us = TIMEOUT_CONTROL 0x00's 2^13 TMCLK
# cycles").
#
# AND THE REGISTER THAT SETS IT HAS NEVER BEEN WRITTEN. `grep -n 'ST_SDHCI_TIMEOUT_CONTROL'` returns the
# define (`entry_storage.c:212`) and ONE READ (`:4233`). `_nidx_tout_ctl = 0x00000000` - the reset value,
# the SHORTEST bound the register can express. The source's own comment says why: the vendor writes it
# only from `sdhci_prepare_data` (`sdhci.c:827-828`), inside `if (data || (cmd->flags & MMC_RSP_BUSY))`,
# and EVERY COMMAND THIS LADDER SENDS IS DATA-LESS. So every response demand in this ladder has been
# racing a 665.2 us bound no rung has ever set.
#
# THE TIMING LADDER, one boot, one counter: CMD0 `_cmd0_ticks = 0x1327` = 4,903 = 255.4 us; CMD1
# `_cmd1_ticks = 0x2824` = 10,276 = 535.2 us and COMPLETED (`_cmd1_complete = 1`,
# `_cmd1_status_any = 0x1`, `_cmd1_any_polls = 0x4d4` = 1,236); CMD2 12,770 = 665.2 us and CMD3 12,772 =
# 665.3 us, BOTH TIMED OUT. CMD1's 48-bit response arrives 130 us INSIDE the bound - the narrowest margin
# in the ladder, and why CMD1 is the one command that completes.
#
# AND THE ARITHMETIC, WITH ITS ASSUMPTION NAMED. One 48-bit response added 5,373 ticks (10,276 - 4,903).
# A 136-bit response is 88 bits more, so at the same measured per-bit rate - THE ASSUMPTION; the rate is
# not separately measured - it lands 88 x (5,373/48) = 9,850 ticks after CMD1's, at 20,126 ticks
# = 1,048.2 us against a 665.2 us bound, i.e. the bound is 63 per cent of what is needed. The rate that
# implies is 5.83 us/bit = 171.5 kHz against rung 6's configured 400 kHz (2.5 us/bit) and THIS STEP DOES
# NOT EXPLAIN THAT. The conclusion survives either rate: at 400 kHz a 136-bit response still needs 340 us
# of shifting on top of CMD1's 535.2 us = 875 us, still past the bound.
#
# WHY CMD3 FAILS IS A DIFFERENT QUESTION AND THE ARITHMETIC DOES NOT EXPLAIN IT. CMD3's 48-bit response
# should land at about CMD1's 535.2 us - same length, same clock, same window shape - and it does not.
# The claim this record offers is the protocol's own and it is NAMED AS A CLAIM, NOT MEASURED: a card
# enters IDENT state only by accepting CMD2, and CMD3 is only accepted in IDENT. CMD2 has never
# completed, so the card has never entered IDENT, so CMD3 gets no answer. Falsifiable cheaply: if CMD2 is
# made to complete and CMD3 still times out, the account is wrong.
#
# SO THE NEXT ARM IS THE FIRST REPAIR THIS LADDER HAS HAD, NOT ANOTHER MEASUREMENT: ONE BYTE STORE to
# `TIMEOUT_CONTROL 0x2E` above 0, before CMD2. `0x01` doubles the bound to 1,330.4 us; `0x02` gives
# 2,660.8 us; the register's maximum is `0x0E`. THE PREDICTION IS NUMERIC. Rows: `_cid_complete = 1` AND
# the four words CHANGED (`_cid_raw0..3`, `_cid_resp0..3` - already read, already published, no new cell
# needed) is THE CID TAKEN; `_cid_complete = 1` with the words unchanged is the fifth row 793 section 5
# named, now on an arm where the bound is not the suspect; `ERR | TIMEOUT` again at a LONGER tick count
# REFUTES the arithmetic and says by how much; `ERR | CRC` returning refutes section 2. Its safety
# surface is one byte, one register, no new address and no new device, and `TIMEOUT_CONTROL` is a
# register the DRIVER ITSELF WRITES on the data path - the vendor's act, not a new one.
#
# WHAT THIS CHANGES ABOUT THE LADDER'S RECORD. (a) 791 section 4 is REFINED, not confirmed and not
# refuted: the immediate CRC requires both conjuncts. (b) 786 section 7's and 788 section 7's anomaly is
# EXPLAINED: the CRC at poll 1 of a window whose 136-bit response cannot have been shifted was NEVER a
# report about the card - it is what this block raises when handed a 136-bit request with its CRC check
# enabled. (c) 790 section 5's `0x40ff8080` discount is UNCHANGED and STRENGTHENED: identical on rungs
# 19, 29, 30 and 31, including one where the block drove the bus and timed out. (d) The frontier moved
# from CMD2 to the TIMEOUT REGISTER.
#
# THE GOAL IS NOT MET. No transfer completes, no filesystem is reached, no mount is made, so
# 「让os可以正常启动并且挂载存储」 is not reached and TWRP-TO-STORAGE STAYS WITHHELD. NO PRESS IS
# AUTHORIZED: rung 31 is spent and no further arm is armed.
#
# 796: THE RUNG-32 ARM - armed-storage-c1f89600, STAGE90_XNU_STORAGE_PROBE=31 (switch VALUE 31 =
# ordinal rung 32). **THIS IS THE FIRST REPAIR ANY RUNG OF THIS LADDER HAS MADE, AND IT IS ONE BYTE
# IN ONE REGISTER.**
#
# THE READING IT ACTS ON IS 795's OWN AND IT IS A NEGATIVE: `TIMEOUT_CONTROL 0x2E` HAD NEVER BEEN
# WRITTEN BY ANY RUNG. grep returns the define (entry_storage.c:212) and ONE READ (:4233), and rung
# 31's own capture read the register back as `_nidx_tout_ctl = 0x00000000` - the RESET VALUE and the
# SHORTEST bound the register can express. The vendor writes it only from `sdhci_prepare_data`
# (sdhci.c:827-828), inside `if (data || (cmd->flags & MMC_RSP_BUSY))`, and EVERY COMMAND THIS LADDER
# SENDS IS DATA-LESS. So every response demand in this ladder has been racing a 665.2 us bound no rung
# ever set, and 795 section 1 measured that constant twice in one boot: CMD2 `_cid_ticks = 0x31e2` =
# 12,770 = 665.2 us and CMD3 `_nidx_ticks = 0x31e4` = 12,772 = 665.3 us.
#
# THE ACT: one body reads the byte, one body stores a compile-time constant into it, and the constant
# is `ST_SDHCI_TIMEOUT_CMD2 = 0x03u` = 5,321.6 us. Its arithmetic, from 795's own ladder: the reset
# bound is 665.2 us, the field doubles per step, so 0x03 is 5.076x the reset bound and 4.68x the
# 1,048.2 us the record's extrapolation puts a 136-bit response at - AND it stays 225x UNDER the
# driver's own 1.200 s poll bound (sdhci.c's `timeout = 10` in 100 ms units), which is the other end
# this value must not cross: at or above 0x0B the device timeout stops being observable at all because
# the ladder's own poll gives up first. The two `_Static_assert`s in entry_storage.c put those two
# ends on the constant at COMPILE TIME (`>= 0x01`, `<= 0x0E`, and the field's own high nibble clear).
#
# THE TWO BODIES ARE BODIES OF THEIR OWN, and that is the same shape 787 used for CMD1's window:
# `st_tout_open` (0x8000de60, 124 bytes) and `st_tout_restore` (0x8000e250, 76 bytes), both
# `noinline, noclone`, each called from `st_cmd_path` and nowhere else. Their device surface is
# `TIMEOUT_CONTROL 0x2E` AS A BYTE and NOTHING ELSE, measured out of the linked image rather than
# asserted: `ldrb r4, [r5, #46]` / `strb r3, [r5, #46]` with `mov r3, #3` in the open, and
# `strb r4, [r3, #46]` / `ldrb r1, [r3, #46]` in the restore. `0x2E` is one byte below
# `SOFTWARE_RESET 0x2F` (rung 4 writes it) and one byte above `CLOCK_CONTROL 0x2C` (rung 6 writes it)
# - two registers this ladder HAS written - so a body that drifted one offset would write a register
# with an entirely different meaning, which is why xnu_entry_796 asserts the offset and the width and
# not merely the address.
#
# SIX KEYS, and they are the window's own state and not a new measurement of the bus: `_tout_calls`
# (the open ran), `_tout_was` (the byte the register held - THE CONTROL, expected 0 on a first run),
# `_tout_wrote` (the constant), `_tout_held` (the readback, expected 3), `_tout_wrote_back` (the byte
# put back), `_tout_readback` (the readback after the restore, expected 0). `_tout_was = 0` beside
# `_tout_held = 3` is the repair VISIBLE; `_tout_was = _tout_held = 0` would be an arm whose store
# never landed and whose every other cell reads exactly as rung 31's did, which is the one failure a
# log cannot otherwise show.
#
# THE WINDOW IS THE CMD2 INTERVAL AND CMD3 IS DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE IT. Read out of the linked image:
# open at 0x8000ed20, the gate's refusal-path close at 0x8000ed70, CMD2's call at 0x8000edb8, the
# CMD2-path close at 0x8000edc8, CMD3's call at 0x8000ede8. **The close is TWO CALLS IN THE IMAGE
# WHERE THE SOURCE HAS ONE**, and that is GCC duplicating the tail of the `if/else` that holds CMD2
# into both of the gate's arms - each path runs exactly one of them. xnu_entry_796 asserts the count
# as a SHAPE (1 open exactly; 1 to 3 closes) and the POSITIONS over every line: every open above
# CMD2, the LAST close below CMD2, and every close above CMD3. **The first draft of the clause
# demanded exactly one close and refused the build**; the refusal was right about the source and wrong
# about the image, and it is recorded in the clause itself rather than silently relaxed.
#
# CMD3 STAYS AT THE RESET BOUND ON PURPOSE, and that is a deliberate part of the arm. CMD3's 48-bit
# response fits inside 665.2 us (795 section 6), so CMD3 is the independent test of 795 section 6's
# protocol claim - a card enters IDENT only by accepting CMD2, and CMD3 is only accepted in IDENT.
# A window that covered CMD3 as well would give CMD3 the same help CMD2 is getting and the two rows
# would stop being separable. **The falsification is cheap and named: if CMD2 is made to complete and
# CMD3 STILL times out, 795 section 6's account is wrong.**
#
# THE ANSWER SPACE, and the prediction is NUMERIC rather than a direction:
#   `_cid_complete = 1` AND the four words CHANGED   THE CID IS TAKEN. 793 section 1's row 1a.
#                                                    `_cid_raw0..3` and `_cid_resp0..3` are already

# WHAT THIS CHANGES ABOUT THE LADDER'S RECORD. (a) The frontier moves from the CMD2 command to the
