# 798: THE RUNG-32 PRESS - THE REPAIR RAN AND THE BOUND DID NOT MOVE, SO `TIMEOUT_CONTROL 0x2E` IS NOT
# WHAT ENDS THIS LADDER'S COMMANDS; AND CMD1 IS SENT ONCE WHERE THE DRIVER LOOPS.
#
# ONE PRESS SPENT, authorized by the operator BEFORE the gate was run. One gate (exit 0, 608 lines),
# one runner (EXIT 0), one `fastboot boot`, nothing flashed, nothing written to storage, no reboot;
# `33e80afe` absent from BOTH device lists at fire time; capture
# out/stage90/captures/rung32-tout-20260928-081329-{last_kmsg.txt,gate.log,run.log}, archived by hand,
# last_kmsg 633,759 B sha256 0e33bbcd4950cb037ec3597078ade6a7fdd01b8f3676619ebd7cce9f9ae4de7a.
# THE MACHINE STAYED UP: `_post_end_calls = 0x7`, `_post_elapsed = 0x06df35b6` = 6004.8 ms at
# `_post_cntfrq = 0x0124f800` (19.2 MHz), so the 6000 ms deadline FIRED and the OS idled the whole
# window. Runner's verdict 7 PASS / 1 FAIL / 3 UNREAD COUNTED PER CRITERION (14/2/6 as lines, the block
# printing twice - the gate's reading of the previous capture and the runner's of this one), the single
# FAIL the known `seam_sp ... is not sleh_sp-8` criterion: IDENTICAL to rungs 29, 30 and 31, so this
# press added no failure.
#
# (1) THE REPAIR RAN, AND THE SIX NEW CELLS SAY SO. `_tout_calls = 0x1`, `_tout_was = 0x0` - THE
# REGISTER HELD ZERO, the reset value, exactly as predicted - `_tout_wrote = 0x3`, `_tout_held = 0x3`
# (THE BLOCK HELD WHAT WAS WRITTEN), `_tout_wrote_back = 0x0`, `_tout_readback = 0x0`. So the window
# opened, the byte went 0 -> 3 and was put back, and the one failure 796 section 4 said the rest of the
# log cannot show - a store that never landed - DID NOT HAPPEN.
#
# (2) THE HEADLINE: THE BOUND DID NOT MOVE BY ONE TICK-TIME. Rung 31 ran CMD2 under `0x00` = 665.2 us
# and read `_cid_ticks = 0x31e2` = 12,770; rung 32 ran it under `0x03` = 5,321.6 us, EIGHT TIMES the
# bound, and read `_cid_ticks = 0x31e4` = 12,772 = 665.3 us, with `_cid_status_any = 0x00018000`
# (`ERR | TIMEOUT`) at `_cid_any_polls = 0x705` = 1,797 on both arms, `_cid_err = 0x00010000`,
# `_cid_complete = 0`. **`TIMEOUT_CONTROL 0x2E` DOES NOT GOVERN THIS EVENT.** The SDHCI specification's
# timeout register scales the DATA timeout; the command response timeout is fixed in the block. 795
# section 5 built the arm on the assumption that this register sets the bound the ladder has been
# hitting, and THIS PRESS IS THE MEASUREMENT THAT SAYS IT DOES NOT. It is the pre-registered refutation
# row and it arrived in the STRONGER form: 796 section 8 named "ERR | TIMEOUT again, at a LONGER tick
# count"; what came back is the SAME tick count, so it refutes the MECHANISM and not merely the
# arithmetic. And 795 section 5's extrapolation about where a 136-bit response would land is UNTOUCHED
# AND UNTESTED - the card is not answering at all, so no response ever raced the bound.
#
# (3) AND IT IS A CLEAN ONE-VARIABLE COMPARISON, MEASURED. Rung 31 carries 481 storage keys and rung 32
# 487, and the six that exist only on rung 32 are the `_tout_*` pair's cells above. Every other cell is
# identical to within timer jitter: `_cid_status_any` `0x00018000` on both; `_cid_word`/`_cid_flags`
# `0x0201`/`0x03` on both; `_cid_raw0..3` `0x0040ff80 / 0x80000000 / 0 / 0` and `_cid_resp0..3`
# `0x40ff8080 / 0 / 0 / 0` on both; `_cmd0_ticks` 4,903 -> 4,901; `_cmd1_any_polls` 1,236 -> 1,238 with
# CMD1 COMPLETING AGAIN; `_nidx_ticks` `0x31e4` -> `0x31e2`. So the press isolated exactly one variable
# - the timeout window - and the variable did nothing.
#
# (4) A DEFECT THIS STEP FOUND IN ITS OWN PREDECESSOR, AND IT IS A GUARD THAT LEAKED. 796 section 1 and
# section 3 state that value 31 sends CMD2's `ST_MMC_RSP_R2` - word `0x0209` - and that "rung 31 sent
# `0x0201` and this arm does NOT". THAT IS FALSE. The capture reads `_cid_word = _cid_word_read =
# 0x00000201` and `_cid_flags = 0x00000003`: rung 32 sent the CRC-DROPPED word. The source is
# unambiguous - entry_storage.c:3328's guard is `#if STAGE90_XNU_STORAGE_PROBE >= 30`, and the two
# `st_all_send_cid` calls at :3348-3353 select on it - so EVERY value at or above 30 inherits rung 31's
# constant. Rung 32 is a STRICT SUPERSET of rung 31's act: the NOCRC flag AND the timeout window.
# **AND THE CLAUSE FAMILY DID NOT CATCH IT, BECAUSE IT WAS NEVER ASKED TO**: `xnu_entry_792` asserts the
# flags register is `#3` and is itself guarded `>= 30`, so at value 31 it asserts `#3` - which the source
# also builds - AND PASSES. The check was right about the image and the PROSE was wrong about the arm;
# this is the m-class "a claim in a document no check reads" again, and the tell is that the check and the
# sentence disagreed and NOTHING COMPARED THEM. The reading in (2) is NOT weakened - the leak made the
# comparison cleaner, since rungs 31 and 32 then differ in the timeout window and nothing else - but
# 796's ANSWER SPACE is: its row 4, "ERR | CRC returning refutes 795 section 2", COULD NOT HAVE FIRED,
# because the CRC flag was not carried.
#
# (5) CMD1 IS SENT ONCE, AND THE GATE BELOW IT READS THE DRIVER'S OWN CONDITION BACKWARDS - and this is
# the finding the press made available, and it is not about the timeout register at all. THE DRIVER
# LOOPS (`mmc_ops.c:141-166`): `for (i = 100; i; i--)` with `err = mmc_wait_for_cmd(...)` inside and
# `mmc_delay(10)` between passes, exiting on `if (cmd.resp[0] & MMC_CARD_BUSY) break;` at `:157` - so the
# driver PROCEEDS WHEN BIT 31 SETS, the card having finished power-up, under the comment "otherwise wait
# until reset completes". THE LADDER SENDS ONCE: `entry_storage.c:4702` is a single
# `st_send_command(ST_CMD_OP_SEND_OP_COND, 0u, ST_MMC_RSP_PRESENT, &c1)` with no loop. AND THE LADDER
# TESTS THE OPPOSITE: `entry_storage.c:4785` is `if (c1.sent != 0u && (c1.resp & ST_MMC_CARD_BUSY) ==
# 0u)` - bit 31 CLEAR proceeds to CMD2. The constant's own comment at :2197 cites `mmc_ops.c:158`'s
# condition and the comment above the gate says "the condition is the DRIVER's, read in the direction the
# driver reads it"; BOTH SENTENCES ARE FALSE against `mmc_ops.c:157`, and both are m-class claims in
# comments no check reads. AND THE MEASURED VALUES PUT THE LADDER ON THE WRONG SIDE OF THAT TEST:
# `_cmd1_resp = 0x40ff8080`, and `0x40ff8080 & 0x80000000 = 0`, so the busy bit is CLEAR, so THE DRIVER'S
# LOOP WOULD NOT HAVE EXITED - it would have retried 99 more times. The ladder proceeded, and
# `_cid_gated = 0` says so. **SO CMD2 IS PUT ON THE BUS FOR A CARD THAT HAS NEVER REPORTED POWER-UP
# COMPLETE, AND THE CARD DOES NOT ANSWER.** That is what the 665.2 us is: the block's fixed response
# window expiring over a silent card - not a bound a register can move, which is exactly what (2)
# measured with the register. And it explains 795 section 6 without the protocol claim: CMD1 is answered
# because a card answers CMD1 WHILE it initializes (that is what the retry loop is for), and CMD2 is not
# answered because the card is not in READY. 795 section 6 reached the right SHAPE from the wrong
# DIRECTION: the reason CMD3 also fails is one step earlier than it said, at CMD1. THE CAVEAT, NAMED:
# `0x40ff8080` may not be a real OCR at all (790 section 5, 787 section 6 - it is byte-identical on arms
# whose window was closed). THE NEXT ARM IS SOUND EITHER WAY.
#
# (6) THE NEXT ARM IS THE FIRST TIME THIS LADDER PORTS THE DRIVER'S OWN CONTROL FLOW: the
# `mmc_send_op_cond` loop - send CMD1 up to N times with the driver's own 10 ms delay, exit when
# `resp[0] & MMC_CARD_BUSY` SETS, and publish two cells the ladder does not have: HOW MANY SENDS IT TOOK
# and WHETHER THE BIT EVER SET. Its four rows: the bit sets on some send k = THE CARD FINISHES POWER-UP
# and the ladder has been sending CMD2 too early since rung 16, after which 793 section 1's row 1a
# becomes live; the bit NEVER sets over the full count puts the subject on POWER AND CLOCK (784's rails
# are RPM resources with no `reg`) and NOT on the command sequence; the response CHANGING between sends
# separates a real OCR from a static pattern WITHOUT knowing which it is; and the response BYTE-IDENTICAL
# every send extends 790 section 5's discount to every arm.
#
# (7) THE GOAL IS NOT MET. No transfer completes, no filesystem is reached, no mount is made, so
# 「让os可以正常启动并且挂载存储」 is not reached and TWRP-TO-STORAGE STAYS WITHHELD. `_cid_complete = 0`
# and the eight RESPONSE words are the nine-arm pattern, so 793 section 1's row 1a DID NOT FIRE. NO PRESS
# IS AUTHORIZED BY THIS STEP: rung 32 is spent and no arm is armed.
#
# (8) OWED, AND NAMED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE INFERRED: entry_storage.c:3328's `>= 30` guard should be
# `== 30` or the record must say value 31 is a containment (COST); 796 sections 1, 3 and 8's sentences
# about `0x0209` are false (COST); the CMD1 loop of (6) is the next arm, pre-registered and NOT built;
# TIMEOUT_CONTROL's real scope is unmeasured on this ladder; the effective bit rate 171.5 kHz against
# rung 6's configured 400 kHz (795 section 10) is untouched and now more pointed; CMD9's `MMC_RSP_R2`
# (797 section 6); and the six live-prose corrections of 797 section 1.
# 800: THE RUNG-33 ARM - armed-storage-ce2f589c, STAGE90_XNU_STORAGE_PROBE=32 (switch VALUE 32 =
# ordinal rung 33). **THE FIRST RUNG WHOSE ACT IS THE DRIVER'S OWN CONTROL FLOW RATHER THAN ONE OF ITS
# CONSTANTS.**
#
# THE READING IT ACTS ON IS 798 section 5's, AND THE PRESS THAT MADE IT IS THE ONLY REASON THIS RUNG
# EXISTS. The rung-32 press found that `TIMEOUT_CONTROL 0x2E` does not govern the command response
# timeout, and then handed over a finding that is not about a register at all: **the driver calls CMD1
# TWICE and this ladder calls it once, and the gate below the one call reads the driver's own test
# BACKWARDS.** `drivers/mmc/core/mmc_ops.c:141-166` is
#
#     for (i = 100; i; i--) {
#             err = mmc_wait_for_cmd(host, &cmd, 0);
#             if (err) break;
#             if (ocr == 0) break;                      /* a probe: one pass */
#             if (cmd.resp[0] & MMC_CARD_BUSY) break;   /* :157 - PROCEED WHEN BIT 31 SETS */
#             err = -ETIMEDOUT;
#             mmc_delay(10);
#     }
#
# - up to 100 sends, 10 ms apart, exiting when `resp[0] & 0x80000000` becomes TRUE. This ladder's
# `entry_storage.c:4702` sends CMD1 ONCE with argument `0u`, and `:4785` gates CMD2 on
# `(c1.resp & ST_MMC_CARD_BUSY) == 0u` - PROCEEDS WHEN BIT 31 IS CLEAR, which is the opposite of the
# line the constant's own comment cites. And the measurement puts the ladder on the wrong side:
# `_cmd1_resp = 0x40ff8080` has bit 31 clear, so the driver's loop would have retried 99 more times and
# this ladder went on to CMD2. **So CMD2 has been put on the bus for a card that has never reported
# power-up complete, since rung 16** - which is what the 665.2 us is.
#
# THE TWO STEPS BETWEEN THE DRIVER'S TWO CALLS DO NOT EXIST IN THIS IMAGE, and that is a grep rather
# than an impression. `mmc.c:1923` is `mmc_send_op_cond(host, 0, &ocr)` - argument 0, and by
# `mmc_ops.c:148-150` that is a SINGLE PASS BY DESIGN. `mmc.c:1951` is
# `host->ocr = mmc_select_voltage(host, ocr)` - the intersection of the card's OCR window with the
# host's. `mmc.c:1359` is `mmc_send_op_cond(host, ocr | (1 << 30), &rocr)` - the LOOPED call, with an
# argument derived from the first response's window and bit 30 set. In `src/entry/`, anchored and
# case-sensitive, `select_voltage` occurs once and IN A COMMENT (the note at `entry_storage.c:4724`
# explaining what it publishes) with no define, no body and no call; the CMD1 argument is the literal
# `0u`; and `1u << 30` occurs once in the whole file as `ST_HC_DLL_RST` (`:258`, a different register),
# so **bit 30 has never been set in any command word this image sends.**
#
# THE ACT, AND IT IS TWO BODIES OF THEIR OWN - the shape 787 and 796 used, so that `st_cmd_path`'s own
# device surface does not move by one offset:
#
#   `st_op_cond_arg`  0x8000de18,  96 bytes  - `(resp & ~0x7F) | (1 << 30)`, nothing else
#   `st_op_cond_loop` 0x8000de78, 320 bytes  - the driver's loop, one `bl <st_send_command>` inside it
#
# both `noinline, noclone`, each called from `st_cmd_path` and nowhere else. **THEIR DEVICE SETS ARE
# EMPTY, AND THAT IS MEASURED OUT OF THE LINKED IMAGE AND NOT ASSERTED**: the derived argument is a
# function of the WORD the caller passes and of nothing the block holds, and the loop's only device act
# is the command it sends, which belongs to `st_send_command` - whose own body and own clause are
# unchanged and whose `st_cmd_path` call count is still asserted to be exactly two (the loop's call is
# inside the loop's body, not in `st_cmd_path`'s). **NO STORE TO ANY REGISTER IS ADDED BY THIS RUNG.**
#
# THE FOUR COMPILE-TIME CONSTANTS, and every one of them is asserted out of the image by
# `xnu_entry_799` rather than trusted from the source:
#
#   `ST_OP_COND_OCR_CLR     0x0000007Fu`  - `mmc.c:1943-1948`'s `ocr &= ~0x7F`, emitted as `bic #127`
#   `ST_OP_COND_BIT30       0x40000000u`  - `mmc.c:1359`'s `(1 << 30)`, emitted as `bic`/`orr`
#   `ST_OP_COND_SEND_MAX    100u`         - `mmc_ops.c:145`'s `for (i = 100; i; i--)`
#   `ST_OP_COND_DELAY_TICKS 192000u`      - `mmc_ops.c:164`'s `mmc_delay(10)` = 10 ms at 19.2 MHz
#
# EIGHT NEW KEYS, and they are the whole answer space: `_opcond_calls` (the argument body ran),
# `_opcond_from` (the word it derives from), `_opcond_arg` (the word it derived - THE ARM'S ONLY
# NUMBER), `_opcond_loop_calls` (the loop ran), `_opcond_sends` (how many sends it took, 1..100),
# `_opcond_busy_seen` (whether bit 31 EVER set - 798 section 5's own test, run more than once for the
# first time), `_opcond_last_resp` (the last response word), `_opcond_ticks` (the loop's own cost).
#
# **THE PREDICTION IS A NUMBER AND IT IS SHARPER THAN THE RUNG THAT MADE IT POSSIBLE.**
# `_cmd1_resp = 0x40ff8080` already has bit 30 SET and its low seven bits ZERO, so
# `(0x40ff8080 & ~0x7F) | 0x40000000 = 0x40ff8080`: **THE DERIVATION IS A NO-OP ON THIS CARD'S OWN
# WORD, and `_opcond_arg` should equal `_opcond_from` exactly.** A value that differs says the
# derivation moved something the response did not already satisfy, which is the only way this rung can
# report on its own first body at all.
#
# THE COST IS NAMED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED: the worst case is 100 sends plus 99 ten-millisecond
# delays, and at the measured 665.2 us per timed-out command that is about **1.06 s added to the
# storage probe** - spent inside `entry_storage_probe` at the OS's idle-exit, where the run's own
# deadline is 6,000 ms (`_post_elapsed`). A run that spans the whole loop is a run whose window shrank
# by that much, and `_opcond_ticks` is the cell that measures what it actually cost.
#
# FOUR ROWS, and the first is the one that would open the ladder:
#
#   (1) `_opcond_busy_seen = 1` on send k <= 100 - **THE CARD FINISHES POWER-UP AND THE LADDER HAS BEEN
#       SENDING CMD2 TOO EARLY SINCE RUNG 16**, and the send count k is a number no arm has carried.
#   (2) `_opcond_busy_seen = 0` over the full 100 sends - the card is not powering up on this path at
#       all, which puts the subject on POWER AND CLOCK (784's rails are RPM resources with no `reg`)
#       and NOT on the command sequence.
#   (3) `_opcond_last_resp` DIFFERS between sends - the block is reading something that MOVES with each
#       CMD1, which separates a real OCR from a static pattern without needing to know which it is.
#   (4) `_opcond_last_resp` byte-identical every send, and equal to `_cmd1_resp` - `0x40ff8080` is a
#       static pattern and 790 section 5's discount extends to every arm.
#
# THE CLAUSE FOUND TWO DEFECTS IN ITS OWN FIRST DRAFTS, AND BOTH ARE WORTH THE SENTENCE.
# (a) `objdump -d` annotates every immediate with its own comment field, so the instruction that clears
# the low seven bits reads `bic r3, r3, #127    ; 0x7f`. The first draft matched `#127` ANCHORED AT END
# OF LINE, which objdump never emits, and the clause REFUSED A BUILD THAT DID EXACTLY WHAT THE ARM SAYS
# - loud, because the pattern is in a `||`-refusal, and it would have refused every future value-32
# build too. The repair strips objdump's comment field rather than loosening the anchor, because a
# loosened anchor is the check that also matches `#1274`.
# (b) The probe whose response the argument is derived from is CMD1, the **LAST** of `st_cmd_path`'s
# two `bl <st_send_command>` sites, and the first draft took the FIRST - which is CMD0's line. The
# assertion was true and the sentence printed beside it would have named the wrong command, which is
# the m-class this project keeps catching. The last is taken now, and the `== 2` assertion further down
# is what makes "the last" unambiguous. **The clause also asserts the EXIT TEST'S DIRECTION** - one
# sign-conditioned branch (`blt`/`bmi`) leaving the loop, which is what `(resp & 0x80000000) != 0`
# compiles to - because that direction is 798 section 5's whole subject and a differently-lowered test
# refuses the build for a human to read rather than passing on an assertion that no longer means
# anything.
#
# CONTAINMENT, MEASURED ON ALL ELEVEN MEMBERS OF THE RUNG BELOW. The value-31 build from this same
# source is TEN OF ELEVEN MEMBERS BYTE-IDENTICAL to the SPENT rung-32 park
# `out/stage90/frozen/armed-storage-c1f89600/` - `stage90-qcdt.img` `bda29ed1...` and `xnu_arm_entry.bin`
# `c1f89600...` included, i.e. the entry image REPRODUCED byte for byte - and the eleventh is
# `xnu_arm_entry-sources.txt`, which records source files BY CONTENT and must move when the tools are
# edited: exactly two of its 28 lines, `build_entry.sh` and `entry_storage.c`, the two files this step
# touched, with the artifact's own hash line identical and the file set identical at 23 files.
#
# THE ARM'S OWN DELTA, MEASURED AGAINST THE SPENT RUNG-32 PARK:
#   entry `.text` (size -A)  5,335,424 -> 5,335,680   **+256**
#   `xnu_arm_entry.elf`      6,732,464 -> 6,732,528   **+64** (the .text grew 256 and 192 of it was
#                                                     absorbed by page alignment, 796 section 7's own
#                                                     rule that an unchanged size is not a claim)
#   `xnu_arm_entry.bin`      5,552,764 -> 5,552,764   SIZE UNCHANGED, **603,185 bytes differ** - an
#                                                     insertion, not 603,185 edits
#   `stage90-build-config.txt` BYTE-IDENTICAL to rungs 23 through 32 (`6c2b6038...`): no payload switch moved
#   `stage90-qcdt.img`       8,572,928 -> 8,572,928   the boot image the press sends
#
# THE PRESS IS THE OPERATOR'S AND NO PRESS IS SPENT OR AUTHORIZED HERE. The arm is ARMED AND NOT PRESSED,
# its park is `out/stage90/frozen/armed-storage-ce2f589c/` with eleven members verified in place, and the
# press path is the two commands `tools/verify_press_ready.sh` prints, run by hand once each. **THE GOAL
# IS NOT MET BY THIS ARM**: no transfer completes, no filesystem is reached and no mount is made, so

#
# 803: THE RUNG-33 PRESS - THE CARD FINISHES POWER-UP ON THE SECOND CMD1, AND THE CID COMES BACK.
#
# ONE PRESS SPENT, authorized by the operator BEFORE the gate was run. One gate (exit 0, 609 lines),
# one runner (EXIT 0), one `fastboot boot`, nothing flashed, nothing written to storage, no reboot;
# `33e80afe` absent from BOTH device lists at fire time (measured before the gate); capture
# out/stage90/captures/rung33-opcond-20260928-123120-{last_kmsg.txt,gate.log,run.log}, archived by hand,
# last_kmsg 637,213 B sha256 6fe60a12d5b029b34f4bb71fec03c2b38cd2d21f4563ddf677249e848fadecc4.
# Runner's verdict 7 PASS / 1 FAIL / 3 UNREAD COUNTED PER CRITERION, the single FAIL the known
# `seam_sp ... is not sleh_sp-8` criterion: IDENTICAL to rungs 29, 30, 31 and 32, so this press added no
# failure. THE MACHINE STAYED UP: `_post_end_calls = 0x8`, `_post_elapsed` last `0x092a857e` = 8.009 s
# at `_post_cntfrq = 0x0124f800` (19.2 MHz).
#
# (1) THE HEADLINE, AND IT IS 798 SECTION 6's ROW 1. `_opcond_calls = 0x1`, `_opcond_from = 0x40ff8080`,
# `_opcond_arg = 0x40ff8080` (EQUAL to `_opcond_from` - THE DERIVATION IS A NO-OP ON THIS CARD'S OWN
# WORD, exactly as pre-registered), `_opcond_loop_calls = 0x1`, **`_opcond_sends = 0x2`**,
# **`_opcond_busy_seen = 0x1`** - BIT 31 SET, THE CARD REPORTED POWER-UP COMPLETE -
# `_opcond_last_resp = 0xc0ff8080` (= `0x40ff8080 | 0x80000000`, the same OCR with the busy bit now set),
# `_opcond_ticks = 0x340ff` = 213,247 = 11.107 ms. The 100-send bound was NOT approached: the loop
# exited on SEND 2. The arithmetic is exact - 213,247 ticks minus `mmc_ops.c:164`'s `mmc_delay(10)`
# (192,000 ticks) leaves 21,247 ticks = 1,106.6 us FOR TWO COMMANDS, about 553 us each, both inside the
# block's 665.2 us window, which is why both completed. The record named 1.06 s as the worst case; what
# it actually spent is 1.107 ms, 958x less.
#
# (2) AND CMD2 ANSWERED: THE CID COMES BACK AFTER NINE ARMS OF SILENCE. `_cid_complete = 0x1` (was 0x0
# on every arm since rung 16), `_cid_status_any = 0x00000001` (bit 0 SDHCI_INT_RESPONSE, NO ERROR BIT OF
# ANY KIND, against 0x00018000 ERR|TIMEOUT), `_cid_err = 0x0`, `_cid_ticks = 0x49e2` = 18,914 = 985.1 us
# (the command really ran, against 12,772 = 665.2 us of the block's own timeout), `_cid_inhibit_after =
# 0x0` (no longer wedged). THE FOUR RESPONSE WORDS ARE `0x45010053 / 0x44573136 / 0x47014a2f /
# 0xe00bb100` and the `_cid_raw_*` family is the SAME SIXTEEN BYTES SHIFTED ONE, so the two independent
# readings agree. IT DECODES AS A REAL CID: MID `0x45` = 69 = SanDisk, OID `0x01 0x00`, PNM `SDW16G`
# (six ASCII characters), PRV `0x01`, PSN `0x4a2fe00b`, MDT `0xb1`. **793 SECTION 1's ROW 1a IS MET AND
# 793 SECTION 5's FIFTH ROW IS REFUTED IN THE SAME EVENT** - the completion latch fired AND the response
# file filled. **It also retires 790 section 5's and 787 section 6's caveat**: `0x40ff8080` was the
# card's OCR all along, with bit 31 clear because the card had not finished power-up.
#
# (3) AND CMD3 ANSWERED TOO, WITH THE RCA. `_nidx_complete = 0x1`, `_nidx_status_any = 0x00000001`,
# `_nidx_err = 0x0`, `_nidx_ticks = 0x2b22` = 11,042 = 575.1 us, and **`_nidx_resp = 0x00000500` - RCA
# `0x0500`** - with `_nidx_resp_pre = 0x2fe00bb1` (the CID's tail) replaced by it. 795 section 6's
# protocol claim is CONFIRMED in the direction it predicted, and this press supplies the cause it was
# missing: CMD3 failing was always a CONSEQUENCE of CMD2 failing, and neither was the problem - the card
# was not ready, and CMD1 is where readiness is asked for.
#
# (4) THE READING, ONE SENTENCE: every arm from rung 16 through rung 32 was sending CMD2 and CMD3 to a
# card that had not finished power-up, and the ladder's own gate is why. `entry_storage.c`'s CMD2 gate
# tests THE PROBE's response (`c1.resp`, the single CMD1 with argument 0) where the driver tests THE
# LOOP's (`mmc_ops.c:157`). **THE GATE IS NOT MERELY INVERTED; IT IS READING THE WRONG WORD** - the probe
# is a single pass by the driver's own design (`mmc_ops.c:148-150`), so its response says nothing about
# readiness. THE REPAIR IS ONE LINE AND IS NOW MEASURED: gate CMD2 on the loop's result. The 665.2 us
# "timeout" nine rungs chased was never a timeout.
#
# (5) SAFETY, CELL BY CELL. Nothing flashed, nothing written to storage, no reboot; the gate's own last
# line is `booted, never flashed, so no outcome of this run can write to storage.`
# `xnu_live_storage_writes` 0 -> 4 is the same four inherited mode-sequence stores every arm from rung 3
# carries, and NO NEW STORE OF ANY KIND: rung 33's own two bodies have an EMPTY DEVICE SET, asserted out
# of the linked image by `xnu_entry_799` before the press. The 11.107 ms of bus time is the whole of this
# arm's new cost.
#
# (6) ONE DIFFERENCE THIS RECORD DOES NOT EXPLAIN, NAMED RATHER THAN GLOSSED: `_post_end_calls` moved
# `0x7` -> `0x8` and `_post_elapsed` last `0x06df35b6` (6.005 s) -> `0x092a857e` (8.009 s), one more
# post-end call and about two more seconds than every arm since rung 24. The storage probe's own delta is
# 11.107 ms and cannot account for 2 s. OWED A CELL, NOT A SENTENCE.
#
# (7) THE GOAL IS NOT MET. No transfer completes, no filesystem is reached, no mount is made; 794
# section 1's BREADTH GAP is untouched and is now the whole distance (four opcodes, no CMD9 define, no
# data path). TWRP-to-storage STAYS WITHHELD.
#
# 804: THE RUNG-34 ARM - armed-storage-7341f5f6, STAGE90_XNU_STORAGE_PROBE=33 (switch VALUE 33 =
# ordinal rung 34). A BUILD, A PARK AND A RECORD: no press, no device action, no runner, no firer,
# `out/` was rebuilt and a new arm is in it.
#
# THE ARM IS THE CMD2 GATE GIVEN THE WORD THE DRIVER ACTUALLY TESTS, AND IT IS THE RUNG 800 NAMED AS
# THE SEPARATE ONE. 799's own comment above `op_busy` says it in the source: "Gating CMD2 on the loop's
# answer is the driver's semantics and it is a SEPARATE rung - one change per rung is this ladder's own
# discipline". The rung-33 press (803) is what made it a measurement rather than a tidy-up, and it did
# so by showing that the old condition is not merely inverted - it reads the WRONG WORD.
#
# (1) WHAT CHANGED, AND IT IS ONE CONDITION. `entry_storage.c`'s CMD2 gate tested
# `c1.sent != 0 && (c1.resp & ST_MMC_CARD_BUSY) == 0` - the PROBE's response - and now tests
# `c1.sent != 0 && op_busy != 0` - the LOOP's result, the value `st_op_cond_loop` has returned since
# rung 33 and which the rung below computes and throws away with a `(void)` cast. The two arms call the
# same bodies, in the same order, at the same place in the driver's own sequence; what changes is WHICH
# WORD DECIDES WHETHER THE SECOND OF THEM RUNS. The split is `#if >= 33 / #else` INSIDE rung 16's own
# guard, so a value below 33 compiles the old condition byte for byte.
#
# (2) WHY THE OLD CONDITION IS WRONG RATHER THAN BACKWARDS. `mmc_send_op_cond` returns after ONE CMD1
# (`mmc_ops.c:148-150`'s `if (ocr == 0) break;`), so the probe's word is what a card that has not
# finished power-up answers: the OCR with bit 31 CLEAR. `(c1.resp & MMC_CARD_BUSY) == 0` is therefore
# TRUE and the old gate PASSES - it fires on the one reading that means "come back later" and passes on
# the reading that means "not ready yet". That is why `_cid_gated` read 0 on every arm from rung 16
# through rung 32 and why all of them put CMD2 and CMD3 on the bus at a card that had not finished
# power-up. The driver's own condition is `mmc_ops.c:157`'s `if (cmd.resp[0] & MMC_CARD_BUSY) break;` -
# the loop leaves when bit 31 SETS - and that is exactly what `op_busy` is.
#
# (3) THE PRESS THAT MEASURED IT. 803's numbers are the two halves in one log: `_opcond_sends = 2` with
# `_opcond_busy_seen = 1` and `_opcond_last_resp = 0xc0ff8080` against `_cmd1_resp = 0x40ff8080` - THE
# SAME OCR DIFFERING BY EXACTLY THE BUSY BIT - and then `_cid_complete = 1` with a real SanDisk
# `SDW16G` CID that nine arms could never read. So the two words are not two readings of one thing:
# they are the answers to two different questions, and the gate was asking the one the driver does not.
#
# (4) TWO NEW CELLS, PUBLISHED ON BOTH PATHS, AND THEY ARE THE REPAIR MADE READABLE.
# `xnu_live_storage_cid_gate_word` is the word the gate tested, read out of the LOOP's own result
# struct; `xnu_live_storage_cid_gate_busy` is the test's own result printed beside its source, the
# shape `_cmd1_resp_busy` already has four lines above. On a row where the card became ready the word
# differs from `_cmd1_resp` by exactly the busy bit; on a row where the loop never saw the card out of
# reset the two are EQUAL and `_cid_gated` is 1 - which is the row the old gate could not produce at
# all. `c1.sent != 0` is KEPT so `_cid_gated_reason` still separates 1 (CMD1 never reached the bus)
# from 2 (it did, and the loop never saw the card out of reset); reason 2's MEANING is what moves.
#
# (5) NO NEW STORE, NO NEW ADDRESS, NO NEW WIDTH, NO NEW MEGABYTE, NO NEW DEVICE AND NO NEW KEY OF ANY
# DEVICE REGISTER. The rung-33 arm's two bodies keep their EMPTY device sets, `st_cmd_path`'s device
# surface is rung 14's unchanged, `st_send_command` is still called exactly twice from it, and the two
# arms call the same bodies. `xnu_live_storage_writes` does not move.
#
# (6) THE BUILD CLAUSE IS THE READING, NOT THIS BLOCK: `build_entry.sh` gained `xnu_entry_804`, which
# reads THREE numbers out of the LINKED IMAGE in the window between `st_cmd_path`'s call to
# `st_op_cond_arg` and its call to `st_all_send_cid`, and each one FAILS ON THE SPENT RUNG-33 PARK:
#
#   |                              | value 32 (armed-storage-ce2f589c) | value 33 (this arm) |
#   | ---------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------- |
#   | sign-conditioned branches    | **1** (`bge` at 8000eea8)         | **0**               |
#   | loads from the PROBE's word  | **1** (slot [sp, #188])           | **0**               |
#   | loads from the LOOP's struct | **0**                             | **1** ([sp, #300])  |
#   | the two new key strings      | **0 / 0**                         | **1 / 1**           |
#
# **BOTH SLOTS ARE DERIVED AND NOT TYPED**: the probe's word's slot is the `ldr r0, [sp, #N]` that
# feeds `st_op_cond_arg` (both images load [sp, #188] there), and the loop struct's base is the
# `add r1, sp, #N` that materialises `&c1b` before the `st_op_cond_loop` call (both images say 224) -
# so a frame that shifts moves the numbers with it and the check does not go blind. The `bge` is the
# point: `(x & 0x80000000) == 0` is a SIGN test, and the value-32 image carries exactly one inside this
# window at 8000eea8 - the branch that PASSES when the card reports it has NOT finished power-up.
#
# (7) THE CLAUSE REFUSED IN SILENCE TWICE BEFORE IT PRINTED A NUMBER, AND BOTH ARE WORTH THE SENTENCE.
# (a) `(( _off >= gw_loop_off )) && gw_hi=$((gw_hi + 1))` as the last command of a `while` body: a bare
# arithmetic command returns 1 when the comparison is false, and this script runs `set -e`, so the
# first offset BELOW the base ended the build with NO MESSAGE. (b) `x=$(... | grep -oE ...)` and
# `x=$(grep -c ... || true)`'s absence: `grep` exits 1 when it matches nothing and `grep -c` exits 1
# WHEN THE COUNT IS ZERO - which is this clause's GOOD case - so the substitution ended the same way.
# Every pipeline in the clause now carries `|| true` and the emptiness is handled as a refusal with a
# cause. Both are 692's class: a failure reported by the wrong producer, or by none.
#
# (8) CONTAINMENT, MEASURED ON ALL ELEVEN MEMBERS OF THE RUNG BELOW. The value-32 build from THIS SAME
# SOURCE is TEN OF ELEVEN MEMBERS BYTE-IDENTICAL to the SPENT rung-33 park
# `out/stage90/frozen/armed-storage-ce2f589c/` - `xnu_arm_entry.bin` `ce2f589c...` and `stage90-qcdt.img`
# `2c9c2492...` included, i.e. THE ENTRY IMAGE REPRODUCED BYTE FOR BYTE AT VALUE 32 - and the eleventh
# is `xnu_arm_entry-sources.txt`, which records sources BY CONTENT and must move when the tools are
# edited: EXACTLY TWO OF ITS 28 LINES, `build_entry.sh` and `entry_storage.c`, the two files this step
# touched, with the artifact's own hash line identical and the file set identical at 23 files. The
# `#else` branch is what buys this: it is the old condition, verbatim.
#
# (9) THE ARM'S OWN DELTA, MEASURED AGAINST THE SPENT RUNG-33 PARK:
#   entry `.text` (size -A)  5,335,680 -> 5,335,744   **+64**
#   `xnu_arm_entry.elf`      6,732,528 -> 6,732,528   SIZE UNCHANGED (Total 5,934,887 -> 5,934,951, +64)
#   `xnu_arm_entry.bin`      5,552,764 -> 5,552,764   SIZE UNCHANGED, **546,395 bytes differ** - an
#                                                     insertion, not 546,395 edits
#   `stage90-build-config.txt` BYTE-IDENTICAL to rungs 23 through 33 (`6c2b6038...`): no payload switch
#                                                     moved
#   `stage90-qcdt.img`       8,572,928 -> 8,572,928   the boot image the press sends
#   `xnu_arm_entry-config.txt` TWO LINES move: the artifact's own hash, and STORAGE_PROBE 32 -> 33
#
# (10) AND THE ARM IS REPRODUCIBLE: the value-33 build was run twice (once before the containment
# build, once after it) and BOTH RUNS' ELEVEN MEMBERS ARE BYTE-IDENTICAL TO THIS PARK, so the park is
# the build of the tree in front of it and not a lucky copy.
#
# THE PRESS IS THE OPERATOR'S AND NO PRESS IS SPENT OR AUTHORIZED HERE. The arm is ARMED AND NOT
# PRESSED, its park is `out/stage90/frozen/armed-storage-7341f5f6/` with eleven members verified in
# place, and the press path is the two commands `tools/verify_press_ready.sh` prints, run by hand once
# each. **THE GOAL IS NOT MET BY THIS ARM**: no transfer completes, no filesystem is reached and no
# mount is made, and 794 section 1's breadth gap (four opcodes, NO CMD9 DEFINE, no data path) is the
# whole distance - CMD9's `MMC_RSP_R2` is the next command in the driver's order and the breadth gap's
# first body, and THIS rung is what makes it reachable. So 「让os可以正常启动并且挂载存储」 is not
# reached and **TWRP-TO-STORAGE STAYS WITHHELD**.

# 808: THE CITATION THE TREE GREW OUT FROM UNDER - a check whose baseline is GIT. NO ARM MOVED: this
# step added `tools/check_line_citations.py`, wired it into `make check`, and appended this block.
# `out/` was NOT written - nothing under it is newer than the step's start, the park
# `out/stage90/frozen/armed-storage-7341f5f6/` verifies 11 file(s), and all ELEVEN live members'
# sha256 values agree with the `armed-storage-7341f5f6` lines above. The arm is still ARMED AND NOT
# PRESSED and **THE PRESS IS THE OPERATOR'S**.
#
# WHAT IT CLOSES: 802 section 7 owed "a check that every site citing a line number still resolves",
# and named the drift by hand - the ladder's CMD2 gate had moved from `entry_storage.c:4785` to the
# line in use now, and the single CMD1 call from the line 798 named to the one in use now. (THE TWO
# NEW NUMBERS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT WRITTEN HERE. See the paragraph below.)
#
# THE OBVIOUS CHECK IS "THE CITATION RESOLVES", AND IT IS WRONG TWICE OVER, BOTH MEASURED BEFORE A
# LINE WAS WRITTEN: (a) 2050 of 2950 citations under `docs/experiments/` name vendor sources - the
# Sdhci, Mmc-ops and cache sources that live in the vendor checkout and are NOT tracked here - so a
# rule against a file that does not resolve would refuse two thousand CORRECT citations and be
# turned off within a step (m775's shape); and (b) resolving a bare basename to the first hit made an
# older prototype read `build.sh:389` as the ARCHIVED snapshot's copy, 165 lines long, and report it
# past the end - **a one-value-two-definitions defect committed by the checker itself**.
#
# SO THE BASELINE IS GIT. A tool that stores its own expected values is a self-written record, and
# `a self-written record is not a constraint` is this project's rule about those. The ground truth
# already exists: the COMMIT THAT WROTE THE CITATION. One `git log -p --reverse -U0` walk per citing
# file dates every token in it, and the cited file at that commit yields what the citation MEANT.
# `MOVED` - the text it named is now at exactly ONE other line - REFUSES and PRINTS the new line.
# `MOVED-AMBIGUOUS` (two or more candidates) and `RE-WRITTEN` and `UNDATED` and `SITE-ABSENT` and
# `PAST-END` REPORT; **guessing among duplicates is the defect the check exists to catch, and 147 of
# `entry_storage.c`'s 4068 distinct line texts occur more than once, so the class is real** - the
# first cut read a duplicated comment fragment as "moved to line 1". `NOT-IN-REPO` is passed over BY
# NAME. A bare basename that two LIVE roots hold is `AMBIGUOUS-PATH` and refuses.
#
# WHAT REFUSES IS ONLY THE PROSE THAT PRINTS FOR THE LIVE ARM - the `rung_para` line and the
# `entry_conseq+=` lines for the rung the artifact's own switch record names - because that is what
# the operator reads at press time. Other rungs' paragraphs, every `#` comment, THIS FILE and
# `docs/experiments/` are REPORTED, not refused: they are historical records and are superseded
# rather than rewritten, the same split `tools/check_count_citations.py` makes.
#
# **AND THIS BLOCK THEREFORE CITES NO LINE NUMBER, WHICH IS DELIBERATE RATHER THAN STYLISTIC.** A
# record is checked by this tool like anything else, and a citation written here that the tree later
# grows past would appear in the check's report the day it drifts - a record that reports itself is
# noise in the very list it is trying to keep meaningful. Where a number is needed, the block above
# names the SITE and lets the check or a reader read the line.

#     high byte of the NEXT word down, under the comment "CRC is stripped so we need to do some
#     shifting" (`sdhci.c:1165-1172`). The ladder's copy is that pattern exactly, and it is how rung
#     33 read a real SanDisk CID. **A builder who read the four words in order would get a wrong
#     128-bit value that still LOOKS like a CSD: no error, no fault, just a number that decodes to
#     nonsense.** So a new arm must CALL that assembler and not re-derive it;

# THE GROUND TRUTH IS THE VENDOR'S OWN TWO EXPRESSIONS, `external/android_kernel_xiaomi_cancro/drivers/
# mmc/host/sdhci.c:1162-1172`: `SDHCI_RESPONSE + (3-i)*4` - **word 3 first**, 12/8/4/0; `<< 8` on each;
# and `if (i != 3)` with `-1` - **the CRC-stripped byte comes from the address ONE BELOW the word, and
# the LAST word takes no byte at all.** The rules are read off those and not invented: a 32-bit offset
# in {12,8,4,0}, an 8-bit offset in {11,7,3}, the descending order within one stimulus segment (broken
# at every `st_send_command`), and the byte one below its own word.
#
# WHY IT CANNOT BE LEFT TO A READING: read the words ascending and the response is reversed; drop the
# byte-below OR and each word loses 8 bits; OR a byte onto the last word and its low byte is stale.
# EVERY ONE OF THEM PARSES, DECODES AND PUBLISHES - no fault, no error, no cell that says "wrong".
#
# THE REFUSALS ARE DEMONSTRATED, NOT ASSERTED: five mutations applied TO COPIES OF THE FILE, never to

# at + 0u"), which is `i != 3` made structural, because an OR onto the offset-0 word has no offset -1
# to name; `+13u` -> OFFSET + PAIR; one word read twice in a segment -> REPEAT. And the UNMUTATED FILE
# IS CLEAN, so the five refusals are the mutation and not the file.

# 812: THE RUNG-35 ARM - armed-storage-6cd6fae8, STAGE90_XNU_STORAGE_PROBE=34 (switch VALUE 34 =

# (1) WHAT CHANGED. ONE new command body in `src/entry/entry_storage.c`, `st_send_csd`, guarded by

# argument `ST_MMC_RCA_1` and flags `ST_MMC_RSP_R2`, opens and closes the same five-bit `INT_ENABLE 0x34`
# window every command body above it opens, publishes the same per-command cell set, and assembles the
# 136-bit response in the driver's word-3-first order. A new opcode define, a new `_Static_assert` on
# the folded word, and the ladder's own bound `> 33` -> `> 34` in `entry_storage.c`; `build_entry.sh`
# gained the `xnu_entry_812` clause. **EVERY GUARD IS A WHOLE-`#if` ALTERNATIVE**: at value 33 and below
# the preprocessor emits the file it emitted before, character for character.
#
# (2) THE ARGUMENT, AND IT IS THE ONE THING THIS RUNG HAD TO SETTLE BEFORE IT COULD BE BUILT. CMD9's
# argument is `card->rca << 16` with `card->rca = 1` ASSIGNED BY THE DRIVER at `mmc.c:1400` - eight
# lines above `mmc_set_relative_addr`, which sends it as `card->rca << 16` (`mmc_ops.c:203`) - and the
# driver's own comment at `mmc.h:38` says the same three things: `MMC_SEND_CSD 9` / `ac [31:16] RCA R2`.
# **AN MMC CARD DOES NOT RETURN AN RCA TO THE HOST.** `mmc.h:32` gives CMD3 the response `R1`, which is
# the 32-bit CARD STATUS: `R1_CURRENT_STATE` is its bits 12:9 (`mmc.h:141`), `R1_READY_FOR_DATA` its bit
# 8 (`mmc.h:142`), and there is NO RCA FIELD AT ANY OFFSET. (An SD card returns one in R6, and even
# there the field is bits 31:16.)
#
# **SO A CLAIM THREE DOCUMENTS CARRIED IS FALSE, AND IT IS THE `one value, two definitions` CLASS.** 811
# section 3 read `_nidx_resp = 0x00000500` as "RCA 0x0500" - i.e. it read bits 15:0 as a field that is
# not one - and 803's block and the `_nidx_resp` sentence in `mi4-the-cid-serial-is-the-phone-serial`
# carry the same reading. The SAME WORD under the vendor's own two macros is
# `R1_READY_FOR_DATA` set with `R1_CURRENT_STATE = 2`, and 2 is `R1_STATE_IDENT` (`mmc.h:149`) - the
# state a card is in AFTER CMD2 and BEFORE a CMD3 it has ACCEPTED. **The ladder's own published cell says
# it too**: `_nidx_state` = `(c3.resp >> 9) & 0xF` = **2** in the committed rung-34 capture, and the
# ladder's own `_nidx_ready` = `(c3.resp >> 8) & 1` is the vendor's `R1_READY_FOR_DATA` bit. Two
# readings of one word, and the one with no basis in either response format is the one the record used.
#
# (3) WHY THAT MATTERS MORE THAN A CORRECTION. CMD9 is legal in STBY and TRAN and not in IDENT - and
# this ladder has never had a CMD3 the card took. So the arm's frontier is NOT CMD9's mechanism (809
# measured that it needs none: the R2 flags, the 136-bit assembler and the RCA argument all exist
# because CMD2 built them); it is that no arm has yet moved the card out of IDENT. **THIS RUNG DOES NOT
# ASSUME OTHERWISE AND DOES NOT GATE ON IT EITHER - IT PUBLISHES IT.** `RESPONSE 0x10` is read BETWEEN
# CMD3 and CMD9 - a moment no rung has read at, which is rung 18's own shape (`st_resp_before`) - and
# published raw and decoded as `_csd_pre_resp` / `_csd_pre_state` / `_csd_pre_ready` /
# `_csd_pre_illegal`. `_csd_pre_state = 3` or `4` is the reading that says the card was listening; 2 says
# it was not, in the same log that reports what CMD9 did with it. **A gate that could not be honest
# about its own precondition would be worse than no gate**: it would turn "the card is not ready for this
# command" into "the command failed", which is the conflation 804's own repair is about one rung down.
#
# (4) THE FOUR WORDS ARE DECODED WITH THE VENDOR'S OWN OFFSETS, WHICH MAKES A CSD ANSWER CHECKABLE FROM
# OUTSIDE THIS IMAGE. `mmc_decode_csd` (`mmc.c:147`) reads `csd->structure = UNSTUFF_BITS(resp, 126, 2)`
# FIRST and returns `-EINVAL` from `mmc.c:162` unless it is non-zero, then
# `csd->mmca_vsn = UNSTUFF_BITS(resp, 122, 4)` (`mmc.c:165`); on the eMMC v4 path this card takes
# (`mmc.c:110`, the same `case 2/3/4` that carries the CID's 32-bit serial) the CSD is v1.2, so
# **`_csd_structure` must read 1 and `_csd_mmca_vsn` must read 4** - two values this ladder did not
# supply and could not have chosen, which is the same free cross-check the CID's `serial` gave against
# `ro.serialno` (811 section 4, 0x4a2fe00b). The rest is `mmc.c:165-196` verbatim: `cmdclass` at 95:84,
# `read_blkbits` at 83:80, `C_SIZE` at 73:62 (which spans the w2/w1 boundary and is written as the
# vendor's own two-piece expression), `C_SIZE_MULT` at 49:47, and `capacity = (1 + C_SIZE) <<
# (C_SIZE_MULT + 2)`. **`_csd_capacity_blocks` IS EXPECTED TO BE A PLACEHOLDER ON THIS CARD AND THAT IS
# STATED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE MISREAD**: a 12-bit C_SIZE cannot express 16 GB, which is why
# `mmc_get_ext_csd` (`mmc.c:201`) says in the vendor's own words that high-capacity cards store a
# "magic" size in the CSD and take the real one from the EXT_CSD - which is CMD8, 809's wall, named one
# rung early by arithmetic.
#
# (5) THE BUILD CLAUSE IS THE READING, NOT THIS BLOCK: `build_entry.sh` gained `xnu_entry_812`, which
# reads the arm out of the LINKED IMAGE. Every number in it was MEASURED before it was written, and the
# whole clause is a statement about the ARTEFACT that 810's check cannot make about the source:
#
#   r0 = **9**      the opcode, `SEND_CSD` (mmc.h:38) - an arm whose opcode moved is not CMD9 at all
#   r1 = **65536**  `ST_MMC_RCA_1` - the value the DRIVER assigns, and the one a reader is likeliest
#                   to get wrong (see (2)); 0 would be CMD9 addressed to no card, and a value taken
#                   from RESPONSE 0x10 would be an argument that came from nowhere
#   r2 = **7**      `ST_MMC_RSP_R2` = `PRESENT | 136 | CRC`, the driver's own flags for CMD9
#                   (`mmc_ops.c:224`'s `MMC_RSP_R2 | MMC_CMD_AC`, with `MMC_CMD_AC` = 0). 3 would be
#                   rung 31's CRC-dropped word; 5 would be CMD3's 48-bit word
#
#   device accesses IN PROGRAM ORDER, distinct:
#     f9824910:ldr  RESPONSE 0x10   the PRECONDITION read, before the window opens
#     f9824934:str  INT_ENABLE 0x34 the window OPENS
#     f9824934:ldr  INT_ENABLE      `_csd_ena_held`
#     f9824938:ldr  SIGNAL_ENABLE
#     f982491c:ldr  RESPONSE 0x1C   WORD 3 - `sdhci.c:1167`'s `(3-i)*4`, the driver's FIRST word
#     f9824918:ldr  RESPONSE 0x18   WORD 2
#     f9824914:ldr  RESPONSE 0x14   WORD 1
#     f982491b:ldrb RESPONSE 0x1B   the CRC byte ONE BELOW word 3
#     f9824917:ldrb RESPONSE 0x17   ONE BELOW word 2
#     f9824913:ldrb RESPONSE 0x13   ONE BELOW word 1
#     f9824930:ldr  INT_STATUS      `_csd_status_post`
#     f9824924:ldr  PRESENT_STATE   `_csd_ps_after`
#   and there is **NO BYTE AT 0x0F** - `sdhci.c:1168`'s `if (i != 3)` gives the LAST word no byte - which
#   is a property visible in an address list and nowhere else. A byte at 0x0F would be a stale byte OR'd
#   onto word 0; 0x0B or 0x1F would be the pairing off by one; an ASCENDING order (0x10, 0x14, 0x18,
#   0x1C) would be the same eight accesses and the 128-bit value with its four words reversed. **All
#   three parse, decode and publish a plausible CSD-shaped number with no fault anywhere**, which is why
#   the SET and the ORDER are both asserted and not only the set.
#
#   AND THE COUNT `f9824910:ldr=2` IS THE OTHER HALF: `RESPONSE 0x10` is read TWICE - once as the
#   precondition, once as word 0 - and a compiler that COMMONED the two loads would leave a count of 1
#   with the order list still reading correctly, publishing a card state taken at the wrong moment with
#   nothing on the wire to show it. **The key strings `_csd_pre_state`, `_csd_op`, `_csd_structure` and
#   `_csd_mmca_vsn` are asserted present** (the precondition is a register and not a load; the two
#   decodes are the self-check), the image side is asserted EMPTY, and `st_cmd_path` is asserted to call
#   `st_send_csd` exactly once.

# **WITHDRAWN, NEVER PRESSED (814): `armed-storage-6cd6fae8` IS NOT AN ARM TO PRESS.** It was armed,

# 814: THE RUNG-35 BUILD, WITHDRAWN AND REPAIRED BEFORE THE PRESS - the CSD fields were decoded off the
# RAW response registers and `UNSTUFF_BITS` is defined over the ASSEMBLED array. A BUILD, A PARK AND A
# RECORD: no press, no device action, no runner, no firer.
#
# (1) THE DEFECT, IN ONE SENTENCE. `st_send_csd`'s six field decodes applied the shifts and masks of
# the vendor's `UNSTUFF_BITS(resp, start, size)` to the four RAW `RESPONSE` registers - but `resp[]` in
# that macro is the array `sdhci_finish_command` ASSEMBLES, `resp[i] = (raw_i << 8) | (raw_{i+1} >> 24)`,
# so every field came out ONE BYTE TOO HIGH. The two most visible - `_csd_structure` and `_csd_mmca_vsn`,
# which are the two cells this arm's own outcome table turns on - were read off `raw0`'s TOP byte, the
# one byte the assembler SHIFTS OUT.
#
# (2) IT IS MEASURED AGAINST AN ANSWER ALREADY IN THIS RECORD. The rung-34 press published the CID's
# four raw words AND its four assembled words, and 811 section 4 decoded the second set into the phone's
# own `ro.serialno`. The vendor's macro over each set:
#
#     field                          ASSEMBLED words        RAW words
#     manfid   UNSTUFF_BITS(120,8)   0x45  (SanDisk)        0x00
#     prod_name[0..5]                "SDW16G"               " SDW16"
#     serial   UNSTUFF_BITS(16,32)   0x4a2fe00b             0x014a2fe0
#
# `0x4a2fe00b` is `ro.serialno`; `0x014a2fe0` is not a serial number and is not even eight digits. The
# same substitution on the body's own six expressions moves all six: `structure` 1 -> 0, `mmca_vsn`
# 1 -> 0, `cmdclass` 0x445 -> 0x534, `read_blkbits` 7 -> 4, `c_size_mult` 2 -> 6, `c_size` 1241 -> 3268,
# computed on those same words as a stand-in (the fix's own doc, section 3).
#
# (3) WHY IT HAD TO BE FIXED AND NOT MERELY REPORTED. This arm's own closing comment reads: `_csd_complete
# = 1` with `_csd_structure = 1` and `_csd_mmca_vsn = 4` is a CSD and CMD7 is next; `_csd_complete = 1`
# with a structure that is neither 1 nor 2 is **738's stale-word trap, one rung up**. A body reading the
# fields off the wrong bytes does not merely publish wrong numbers - **it publishes a MISLEADING
# VERDICT**, and the verdict it would have published is the one that sends the next rung after a phantom.
# This is `one value, two definitions`; and rung 18's own comment already carried the fact that was
# missed - "the four raw words holding that same 32-bit value ONE BYTE FURTHER ALONG".
#
# (4) THE FIX. The four assembled words are bound to locals `a0..a3` and the six decodes read `a0`/`a1`/
# `a2`. **The four published `_csd_resp*` cells are UNCHANGED IN VALUE** - they were always the assembled
# expressions - so no log key moved and no key was added. Three comment blocks gained the distinction,
# including this rung's own header comment. **NO SWITCH MOVED**: `xnu_arm_entry-config.txt` differs from
# the withdrawn arm's in EXACTLY ONE line, the artifact's own hash, and `stage90-build-config.txt` - the
# payload's own switch record - is BYTE-IDENTICAL (`6c2b6038...`).

# (5) THE CLASS IS NOW A BUILD REFUSAL AND NOT A SENTENCE. `tools/check_response_word_order.py` gained
# **rule 4**: a variable whose whole value is a bare `st_read32(... RESPONSE + K)` for K in {8, 4, 12},
# and an inline read at those offsets, may not be the left operand of `>>`. **OFFSET 0 IS EXEMPT AND
# DELIBERATELY SO** - the vendor's short-response branch reads `resp[0]` straight out of that register
# with no shift, so a right shift of an offset-0 read is the driver's own shape. **MEASURED IN BOTH
# DIRECTIONS BEFORE IT LANDED**: over the whole of `entry_storage.c` - 4,600 lines, seven

# 819: **THE RUNG-35 PRESS — `armed-storage-47c657af` WAS PRESSED AND IT IS SPENT. THE CARD
# ANSWERED CMD9 WITH A CSD, AND THIS ARM'S OWN OUTCOME TABLE WOULD HAVE CALLED IT A FAILURE.** One
# gate exit 0 / 612 lines; one runner exit 0; `fastboot boot` only; nothing flashed; nothing written
# to storage; no reboot commanded; `33e80afe` absent from BOTH device lists, hand-checked immediately
# before the gate (neither log carries that check, and this record says so rather than implying it);
# the phone returned to Android 25 s after the send (the runner's own line, `seen via: adb`).
# Readiness resolved the arm AS THE RECORDED SET before firing: 5 of 5, exit 0. **NOTHING UNDER out/
# THAT THE ARM OWNS MOVED**: `xnu_arm_entry.bin` is still `47c657af...` and `stage90-qcdt.img` still
# `b703a0a5...`. The gate read the image it was asked to verify as `STAGE90_XNU_STORAGE_PROBE=34` with
# `STAGE90_XNU_ENTRY_SHA256=47c657af...` bound to the config, so the bytes sent were the arm's.
#
# Capture `out/stage90/captures/rung35-csd-20260929-003809-last_kmsg.txt` **639,650 B
# sha `ce33dd94b9ceafffe797e4d0a7943e723ef8e836aea000f122a619f66e5806e0`**, archived by hand with
# `...-gate.log` (52,323 B, `a02b7391...`) and `...-run.log` (89,267 B, `e5b72f9b...`) beside it.
#
# (1) THE COMPLETION. `_csd_op = 9`, `_csd_arg = 0x00010000` (`ST_MMC_RCA_1`, the constant the DRIVER
# assigns), `_csd_word = _csd_word_read = 0x00000909`, `_csd_flags = 7` (`ST_MMC_RSP_R2`),
# `_csd_complete = 1` (`INT_STATUS` bit 1), **`_csd_err = 0` with the four command-error bits ENABLED
# (`_csd_ena_wrote = 0x000f0001`)**, `_csd_timeout = 0`, `_csd_any_polls = 0xc4d` with
# `_csd_status_any = 1` on the first poll, and **`_csd_inhibit_seen = 0`** — the block was never
# inhibited, unlike the dead-chain CMD3 of rung 19 whose `CMD_INHIBIT` was asserted at all 1,024
# samples. `_csd_stale = 1` is `INT_STATUS` AS FOUND - the latch's baseline - and NOT a statement about
# the response word; `_csd_clear_wrote = 1` / `_csd_clear_after = 0` is that bit written back.
#
# (2) **ALL FOUR `RESPONSE` REGISTERS MOVED, AND ONE OF THEM HAS A MEASURED BEFORE-VALUE.**
# `_csd_pre_resp = 0x00000500` is `RESPONSE + 0` read by this very body immediately before CMD9, and
# CMD3's own post-read in the same boot publishes `_nidx_raw_post3 = 0x00000500` as well. After CMD9
# that register reads `0xef8a4040`, and `_csd_raw0..3 = 0x00d00f00 0x320f5903 0xffffffff 0xef8a4040`
# are none of CMD3's `0xe00bb102 0x47014a2f 0x44573136 0x00000500`. **A 48-bit response writes
# `RESPONSE + 0` alone; all four moved, so a 136-bit frame was read into all four.** The register did
# not hold a stale word and this is measured, not inferred.
#
# (3) THE READING, ON FIVE CROSS-CHECKS THAT DO NOT DEPEND ON LIKING IT. The four ASSEMBLED words
# `_csd_resp0..3 = 0xd00f0032 0x0f5903ff 0xffffffef 0x8a404000` decode, by an independent 30-line
# implementation of `sdhci_finish_command`'s assembler and `UNSTUFF_BITS`'s bit numbering, to every
# field this arm publishes:
#
#     CSD_STRUCTURE  3     the EMMC structure - `mmc.c:159` rejects only 0, and this file's own
#                          pre-registration said "must read 1", which is the SD family's reading
#     SPEC_VERS      4     `mmc.h:272` CSD_SPEC_VER_4 "Implements system specification 4.0 - 4.1"
#     CCC            0xf5  exactly the eMMC class set (0, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7)
#     READ/WRITE_BL_LEN 9  / 9   512 bytes both ways
#     C_SIZE 0xfff / C_SIZE_MULT 7  ->  capacity = 0x200000 = 2,097,152 = **4096 * 512**
#
# **`4096 * 512` IS THE VENDOR'S OWN LITERAL** - `mmc.c:241`, `if (card->csd.capacity == (4096 * 512))`,
# under the comment at `mmc.c:238` that says high capacity cards store this "magic" size in their CSD.
# Three cells this ladder published reproduce a constant the shipping driver compares against, on a
# part whose CID reads `prod_name = "SDW16G"` - a 16 GB iNAND - in the same capture. And the chain
# around it is the driver's own order, working for the first time: CMD1 (`0x40ff8080`), CMD2 (CID,
# serial `0x4a2fe00b` = this phone's `ro.serialno`), CMD3 (R1 `0x00000500`, ILLEGAL_COMMAND clear),
# CMD9 (the CSD). **Every one of those words is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the previous boot's** - the card's
# answers are deterministic across presses, which is what makes a cross-check against a vendor
# constant worth anything.
#
# (4) **THE ARM'S PRE-REGISTERED TABLE ROW 2 FIRES, AND ROW 2 IS WRONG.** Measured `_csd_complete = 1`
# with `_csd_structure = 3`; the table's second row calls a structure that is neither 1 nor 2 "a
# 136-bit register read that is NOT a response to this command". Two defects:
#   * the table classifies against `{1, 2}` where **`mmc.c:159` rejects only `0`** - `{1,2}` is the SD
#     family's reading of a field this card reads as an eMMC, one value with two definitions, and the
#     ladder encoded the family it is not;
#   * the prose one paragraph earlier (`entry_storage.c:4525`, "`_csd_structure` must read 1") reaches
#     that conclusion from `mmc.c:110`, which is inside **`mmc_decode_cid`** and switches on
#     `cid->mmca_vsn` - the CID's spec version - not on `structure`, which is what `mmc_decode_csd`
#     switches on. Two switch variables in two decoders, read as one.
# **A pre-registration is a claim in a comment with a table drawn round it, and NOTHING CHECKS IT.**
# The arm's six field EXPRESSIONS are now checked (814's rule 4 in `check_response_word_order.py`,
# which refuses the raw-word decode); its one CLASSIFICATION RULE is not checked by anything, and the
# rule is what decides what the press means. The next arm's rows are written from the vendor's own
# predicate - `structure == 0` is the only rejection - and from the fields for the card this is.
#
# (5) FIVE WRONG VENDOR CITATIONS IN THE BLOCK THE READING DEPENDS ON. `entry_storage.c:4645-4650`, the
# field table a reader uses to check (3) by hand, re-measured against
# `external/android_kernel_xiaomi_cancro/drivers/mmc/core/mmc.c`:
#     `mmc.c:173` cmdclass        -> 174
#     `mmc.c:185` read_blkbits    -> 180     (**:185 is WRITE_BL_LEN - A DIFFERENT FIELD**)
#     `mmc.c:175` C_SIZE          -> 177
#     `mmc.c:174` C_SIZE_MULT     -> 176
#     `mmc.c:174-176` the capacity expression (`:4530`) -> 178
# `mmc.c:147`, `:165`, `:162`, `:110`, `:201`, `:165-196` re-measure correct. **A PREVIOUS PASS HAD
# ALREADY AUDITED THIS AREA AND CALLED IT CLEAN** - the block above states that `mmc.c:1400`,
# `mmc.c:1409`, `mmc.c:83`, `mmc.c:120` and the `sdhci.c` ranges "were re-measured and are correct as
# written" - and they were re-measured against a LIST SOMEONE WROTE DOWN, on which these five do not
# appear. An audit that walks a remembered list is not a citation check: m810's shape, a clean verdict
# about the cells that were read, published as a verdict about the file. **OWED TO THE NEXT BUILD CYCLE,
# AND THE COST HAS CHANGED**: 813 and 816 assigned this class to "the next build cycle" for COST - any
# edit to `entry_storage.c` moves `xnu_arm_entry-sources.txt`, a park member, and would have forced a
# withdrawal-and-repark of an arm that was armed and unspent. **The arm is spent and rung 36 edits that
# file regardless, so the repair is now free and lands with the next build.**
#
# (6) CONTAINMENT, MEASURED CELL BY CELL AGAINST THE SPENT RUNG-34 CAPTURE:
#     storage cells        497 -> 555
#     keys lost            **0**
#     keys added           **58**, the entire `_csd_*` family and nothing else
#     values identical     **475**
#     values moved         **22**, every one a free-running quantity - poll counts, tick counts and the
#                          two absolute power-IRQ timestamps - the largest by 5 ticks and most by 1 or 2
# **Not one decision cell moved**: `_cmd1_resp = 0x40ff8080`, `_cid_resp0..3`, `_cid_raw0..3`,
# `_nidx_resp = 0x00000500`, `_cid_gate_word = 0xc0ff8080` and every `_csd_pre_*` cell are identical
# across the two boots. 200 of the 912 non-storage cells moved, which is the entry image's own text
# having grown under 814's repair: the OS's pointers are read out of the image under test and move
# with it.
#
# (7) WHAT THE PRESS DOES NOT SETTLE. Where the card is: `_csd_pre_state = 2` comes from CMD3's R1
# status word read BEFORE CMD9, and a card moves to STBY when CMD3 COMPLETES - so the field may be
# reporting the state the card was in INSIDE CMD3. The press cannot separate "sampled before the
# transition" from "still in IDENT and answered CMD9 anyway", and the pre-registered row 3 rests on the
# second. The vendor's own init runs CMD3 then CMD9 back to back (`mmc.c:1409` -> `:1420`) on this
# device, so the sequence is the shipping driver's - but EXPECTED IS NOT MEASURED. It also does not
# settle whether CMD3's response is CMD3's (the ladder's CMD3 sends `0x030A`, `INDEX` clear - 817): a
# card that had refused CMD3 would be in IDENT, so the CSD is evidence CMD3 was accepted, of the same
# shape and no stronger. And it reaches no block: no CMD8, CMD16, CMD17/18, no filesystem, no mount.
#
# (8) THE FRONTIER IS NOW THE DRIVER'S OWN NEXT COMMAND - **CMD7 `SELECT_CARD`**, `mmc.c:1436`'s
# `mmc_select_card`, whose words are `mmc_ops.c:36-37`: `cmd.arg = card->rca << 16` and
# `cmd.flags = MMC_RSP_R1 | MMC_CMD_AC`. **`MMC_RSP_R1` = `0x031A` IS THE WORD 817 SHOWED THE LADDER
# REMOVED FROM CMD3 AND HAS NOT SENT SINCE RUNG 21**, and it is the SAME FLAGS VALUE `mmc_ops.c:204`
# gives CMD3 - so the next arm is one new command carrying the driver's own word and needs NO NEW
# MECHANISM: a 48-bit response, the arithmetic `st_cmd3_noidx` already runs, and the R1 decode
# (`R1_CURRENT_STATE` `mmc.h:141`, `R1_READY_FOR_DATA` `mmc.h:142`, ILLEGAL_COMMAND bit 22) the CSD body
# already publishes. **It is R1 and NOT R1B** - the vendor does not use the busy bit here, so there is
# no DAT0 busy window to handle. Its three readings: completes with `_err = 0` and state 4 (TRAN) says
# the card was in STBY, CMD7 selected it, AND the INDEX bit is safe on this controller on a live chain;
# completes with ILLEGAL_COMMAND set and state 2 says the card is in IDENT and the CMD3 chain is not
# what it looks like; hangs with `CMD_INHIBIT` asserted and no interrupt says the removal was right and
# is now measured on a live chain. **AND NOTHING IS ARMED**: no build has been made since the press,
# `out/` holds the SPENT rung-35 park, `frozen/` is a record and not a queue, **no arm is armed and no
# press is owed or authorized.**
#
# **THE GOAL IS NOT MET.** 「把基础驱动跑起来」 moved - the storage controller's chain now answers at
# CMD9 and the card's own CSD is in the record - but no transfer completes, no filesystem is reached
# and no mount is made, so 「让os可以正常启动并且挂载存储」 is not reached and **TWRP-TO-STORAGE STAYS
# WITHHELD**: the storage it would be written to is the one thing this ladder has not got working. The
# first clause, 「起码要能进入操作系统」, remains met and is unchanged by this press.

# 819, 2026-09-29 - THE RUNG-36 ARM: `armed-storage-18b0ccf3`, PARKED AND NOT PRESSED.
#
# **AND THIS BLOCK CORRECTS ONE SENTENCE OF THE BLOCK ABOVE IT, BECAUSE THAT SENTENCE IS THE DEFECT
# THIS RUNG'S OWN BUILD CAUGHT.** The 819 block above ends its "what follows" paragraph with
# `**MMC_RSP_R1 = 0x031A IS THE WORD 817 SHOWED THE LADDER REMOVED FROM CMD3...**`. **`MMC_RSP_R1` is
# NOT `0x031A`.** `MMC_RSP_R1` is the FLAG WORD `0x15` - `ST_MMC_RSP_PRESENT | ST_MMC_RSP_CRC |
# ST_MMC_RSP_OPCODE` = `0x01 | 0x04 | 0x10` - and `0x031A` is **CMD3's COMMAND WORD**: opcode 3 in
# bits 15:8 (`0x0300`) with `ST_SDHCI_CMD_FLAGS(MMC_RSP_R1)` = `0x1A` in bits 7:0. Two values, and the
# sentence used one where it meant the other. CMD7 is opcode 7, so **CMD7's command word is `0x071A`**
# - and the FLAG BYTE `0x1A` is the byte rung 21 took the INDEX bit out of, leaving `0x0A`
# (`ST_MMC_RSP_R1_NOIDX`, live CMD3 word `0x030A`). **What 817 measured the ladder removing is a BIT
# FROM A FLAG BYTE, not a word.** The compiler refused the first draft of rung 36's own
# `_Static_assert`, which had copied `0x031A` from the CMD3 assert three blocks up - so this instance
# was caught by the artifact and not by review, and it is `one value, two definitions` (`m819`, and
# `m814`'s sibling) committed in the very paragraph that corrects that class.
#
# **WHAT THIS ARM IS.** Switch VALUE 35 = ordinal rung 36 = **CMD7 `SELECT_CARD`**, the driver's own
# statement at `mmc.c:1436` (`err = mmc_select_card(card);`) immediately after `mmc.c:1420`'s CMD9.
# Its body is `st_select_card` (`mmc_ops.c:26`'s `_mmc_select_card`, non-NULL card): opcode 7
# (`mmc.h:36`, `ac [31:16] RCA R1`), argument `card->rca << 16` (`mmc_ops.c:36`) = the same
# `ST_MMC_RCA_1 0x00010000` CMD3 and CMD9 carry, and flags `MMC_RSP_R1 | MMC_CMD_AC` (`mmc_ops.c:37`)
# = **21**, i.e. `PRESENT | CRC | OPCODE`. It is **R1, not R1b** - no DAT0 busy window.
#
# **THE FLAG VALUE 21 IS THE ARM, and the INDEX bit in it is the second reading.** `sdhci.c:1140-1143`
# maps `MMC_RSP_OPCODE` onto `SDHCI_CMD_INDEX` `0x10`, which has the block compare the response's
# index field against 7 and raise `SDHCI_INT_INDEX` `0x00080000` when it differs. With the bit SET, a
# completion with no error means the frame that arrived IS CMD7's response; with it CLEAR - the live
# CMD3, rung 21 up - a completion means only that a CRC-valid 48-bit frame arrived, which is exactly
# what 813 section 5 could say and no more. **The bit is on THIS rung and not put back on CMD3
# (one rung moves one thing), so CMD3's word stays `0x030A` in the same boot and `_nidx_*` beside
# `_sel_*` is a comparison of the two on one bus.** If this body hangs, the rung has bought 817's
# answer and not CMD7's; the successor drops the bit.
#
# **IT IS THE LADDER'S FIRST UNGATED COMMAND, deliberately.** Every gate below it is a statement about
# the command BELOW (`cid_sent`, CMD2's arrival). CMD7's precondition is the card's state after CMD3 -
# and this file has no cell that measures it: the register read before CMD7 holds the last 32 bits of
# the CSD (`_csd_resp_short = 0xef8a4040`), which is not an R1 and carries no `R1_CURRENT_STATE`. A
# gate on that would be `m812`/`m819` installed as a control-flow decision, so the command goes out
# unconditionally, `_sel_pre_cid_sent` publishes what a gate WOULD have read, and the reading is the
# command's own R1. **Safe because of what CMD7 is**: `ac [31:16] RCA R1`, no data phase, no storage
# write, no register this image can reach - one 48-bit frame on CMD, the same shape as the CMD3 four
# lines up that this ladder sends on every press. Not a brick path.
#
# **THE FOUR OUTCOMES THE PRESS DECIDES, each naming the next act:**
#   `_sel_complete = 1`, `_sel_err = 0`, `_sel_state = 4` (TRAN) -> THE CARD IS SELECTED, the data path
#     opens, CMD8 (`SEND_EXT_CSD`) is next.
#   `_sel_complete = 1`, `_sel_err` carrying `SDHCI_INT_INDEX` `0x00080000` -> a 48-bit frame whose
#     opcode field is NOT 7: the first direct statement this ladder can make about the CMD line, and
#     817's hypothesis answered against it.
#   `_sel_complete = 1`, `_sel_illegal = 1` (bit 22) -> THE CARD ITSELF REFUSED: it is in IDENT and
#     CMD3 was not accepted, whatever its `_nidx_*` cells say.
#   `_sel_complete = 0` with `CMD_INHIBIT` asserted -> the word `0x071A` hangs a live block, which is
#     rung 21's reason MEASURED on a chain that works; the successor drops the bit.
#
# **WHAT THIS ARM'S OWN BUILD PROVED, so the park is not just bytes.** Four measured refusals and one
# declaration, all in `src/entry/build_entry.sh`'s `xnu_entry_819`: `st_select_card` is in the linked
# image at `0x8000ebcc` and loads `r0=#7`, `r1=#65536`, `r2=#21` immediately before its one `bl` to
# `st_send_command` (line 76); its device accesses in program order, distinct, are
# `f982491c:ldr f9824918:ldr f9824914:ldr f9824910:ldr f9824934:str f9824930:ldr f9824934:ldr
# f9824938:ldr f982492e:ldrb f9824924:ldr` - the four RESPONSE words DESCENDING as the freshness
# baseline, the INT_ENABLE window opened after them and closed after the command, and **NO byte below
# any word and NO second word**, because this response is 48 bits and not 136; counts include
# `f9824910:ldr=2` (the four words read on both sides of the command, so `_sel_resp_moved` is a
# comparison of two readings and not of a value with itself) and `f9824934:str=2` (the window closed);
# the image side is EMPTY; `st_cmd_path` calls it once, UNGATED; and the four cell strings
# `_sel_state`, `_sel_illegal`, `_sel_err`, `_sel_resp_moved` are in the linked image.
# `tools/check_response_word_order.py` reads 8 response-reading function(s) and 0 divergences, with
# `st_select_card` the eighth.
#
# **AND FIVE OWED CITATIONS LANDED IN THIS CYCLE, because the COST reason expired** (rung 36 edits the
# file regardless): `entry_storage.c:266` and the prose at `:253` now cite `sdhci.h:162` (measured:
# `#define SDHCI_HOST_CONTROL2 0x3E` is defined exactly once in `external/`, at that line); the five
# wrong `mmc.c` lines in the CSD field table are corrected to `:158` structure, `:174` cmdclass,
# `:180` read_blkbits, `:177` C_SIZE, `:176` C_SIZE_MULT, `:178` the capacity expression; and 813's
# four `sdhci.c:1169-1175` sites (`rsp_present`'s comment and three prose sites) now cite
# `sdhci.c:1162-1175` and `:1162`, the vendor's own `MMC_RSP_PRESENT` guard. **All of them are
# comment-only and it is MEASURED, not assumed**: the entry bin rebuilt after them is BYTE-IDENTICAL
# (`cmp` clean, `18b0ccf3...`), which is this project's linker-fill rule applied as a proof.
#
# **AND THE RUNG-35 ARM'S FALSE OUTCOME TABLE IS REPAIRED IN PLACE.** Rung 35's pre-registration
# classified `CSD_STRUCTURE` against `{1, 2}` and called anything else "a 136-bit register read that is
# NOT a response"; the press answered `3`, a genuine eMMC CSD. The vendor's predicate is `mmc.c:159`'s
# `if (csd->structure == 0)` and nothing else, and it is now `ST_CSD_STRUCTURE_IS_CSD` - **a build

# 821, 2026-09-29 - THE RUNG-36 PRESS. `armed-storage-18b0ccf3` IS SPENT.
#
# **A PRESS, under the operator's authorization asked for and given in this session** (asked with the
# arm parked and verified; the answer was "Press rung 36 now"). ONE gate exit 0 / 613 lines, 0 FAIL;
# ONE runner exit 0. `fastboot boot` only, nothing flashed, nothing written to storage, no reboot
# commanded, `33e80afe` absent from BOTH device lists hand-checked immediately before the gate

# CAPTURE `out/stage90/captures/rung36-cmd7-20260929-012553-last_kmsg.txt` 641,956 B

# the recorded set before the gate: 5 of 5, exit 0.
#
# **THE PRESS ANSWERED TWO QUESTIONS, AND THE FIRST IS 817's.**
#
#   1. **`SDHCI_INT_INDEX` WAS ENABLED AND DID NOT FIRE.** The window is ST_SDHCI_INT_ENABLE_CMD
#      0x000F0001 - bit 0 (RESPONSE) and bits 16, 17, 18, 19, and BIT 19 IS SDHCI_INT_INDEX
#      (`sdhci.h:133`, `SDHCI_INT_CMD_MASK` at `sdhci.h:144-146`) - measured as `_sel_ena_wrote =
#      0x000f0001` and `_sel_ena_held = 0x000f8001` (bit 15 is SDHCI_INT_ERROR, the summary bit the
#      driver's own int_enable already carried). `_sel_err = status_after & ST_SDHCI_INT_CMD_ERR =
#      0x00000000`. **So the block compared the response's Index field against 7 and it MATCHED: THE
#      FRAME THAT ARRIVED IS CMD7's RESPONSE.** That is the attribution 813 section 5 recorded as
#      unreachable ("the block reports that a frame arrived; it does not report who sent it") and the
#      FIRST time this ladder has been able to make it about any command.
#      **AND IT RETIRES RUNG 21's DEVIATION, MEASURED ON A LIVE CHAIN.** 817 read the rung-19 press
#      and the whole archive and argued that the hang which justified removing the INDEX bit was a
#      block still inhibited by a CMD2 that never finished - CMD1 completed on no arm before rung 30 -
#      and that the removal was inherited from an artifact. This press is the positive control that
#      argument never had: same controller, same five-bit window, same chain, the bit ON, and
#      `_sel_complete = 1`, `_sel_inhibit_seen = 0`, `_sel_timeout = 0`, `_sel_err = 0`.
#      **817's hypothesis is refuted and rung 21's reason is gone.** What remains is whether CMD3
#      should carry the bit too - a rung of its own, and NOT the next one.
#
#   2. **THE CARD REPORTS STBY, SO CMD3 WAS ACCEPTED** - which is 819 section 5's first open question.
#      Three cells in ONE boot: CMD3's own response `_nidx_state = 2` = R1_STATE_IDENT (mmc.h:149);
#      the read between CMD3 and CMD9 `_csd_pre_state = 2` = IDENT; and CMD7's own response
#      `_sel_state = 3` = R1_STATE_STBY (mmc.h:150), with `_sel_ready = 1` (R1_READY_FOR_DATA, bit 8)
#      and `_sel_illegal = 0` (bit 22 clear - the card did NOT refuse). The card advanced IDENT -> STBY
#      between the two responses and the only command between them that can do that is CMD3. **So CMD3
#      was accepted, stated as a FIELD rather than as the absence of a refusal** - which 819 section 5
#      said the CSD's arrival could not be.
#      **AND THE CELL DOES NOT SETTLE WHETHER CMD7 LANDED.** R1_STATE_STBY is also what a CMD7 that took
#      no effect would leave, and the field is sampled at response time, before the command's own
#      effect on the JEDEC convention - which is exactly what makes CMD3's 2 and CMD7's 3 read as a
#      TRANSITION rather than as a failure. One reading of one field cannot separate "the card is in
#      STBY because CMD7 has not landed yet" from "the card is in STBY because CMD7 did not land". The
#      row the arm pre-registered for the refusal (`_sel_illegal = 1`) did NOT fire.
#
# **THE COMMAND AS IT WENT OUT, all three values measured:** `_sel_op = 7`, `_sel_flags = 0x00000015` =
# 21, `_sel_arg = 0x00010000`, `_sel_word = _sel_word_read = 0x0000071a`. **And `0x031A` - the value 820
# removed from this record - appears nowhere on this boot's wire**: CMD3 sent `_nidx_word = 0x0000030a`
# with `_nidx_flags = 0x00000005`. The two words are one bit apart in the flag byte (`0x1A` against
# `0x0A`) and an opcode apart, which is what 820's second `_Static_assert` asserts and the press now
# shows.
#
# **`RESPONSE + 0` moved** from the CSD's last word to the R1: `_sel_resp_pre = 0xef8a4040` (the same
# value `_csd_raw3` published in this boot), `_sel_resp_post = 0x00000700`, `_sel_resp_moved = 1`,
# `_sel_resp_is_arg = 0`. That is the direct evidence the frame was read, and it is stated for
# `RESPONSE + 0` and for nothing else.
#
# **RECORDED AND UNEXPLAINED: the other three registers also moved, and what they moved to is not
# anything this image writes.** Before (`_sel_raw_pre*`, which reproduce this boot's `_csd_raw*` cell for
# cell - the CSD's RAW words): +0x0C 0x00d00f00, +0x08 0x320f5903, +0x04 0xffffffff, +0x00 0xef8a4040.
# After (`_sel_raw_post*`): +0x0C 0x8a40401e, +0x08 0xffffffef, +0x04 0x0f5903ff, +0x00 0x00000700. The
# three that moved hold **the CSD's ASSEMBLED words** - `_csd_resp1 = 0x0f5903ff` at +0x04,
# `_csd_resp2 = 0xffffffef` at +0x08, and `_csd_resp3 = 0x8a404000` at +0x0C except for its LOW BYTE,
# which reads 0x1e where the assembled word has 0x00. **No store to `RESPONSE` exists anywhere in this
# image** (the build clause asserts the body's device surface is four reads and the window, and the
# access census refuses an unlisted access), so this is either something the BLOCK does to its own
# response registers when a 48-bit response arrives or an artifact of how those registers behave after a
# 136-bit read. **This arm cannot tell those apart and does not claim to.** It is written down because it
# is 814's shape one rung up - an assembled value and a raw value in the same register file - and
# because a reader comparing `_csd_resp*` against a later `_sel_raw_post*` would otherwise read a
# coincidence as a law. **The 0x1e is in no cell and no comment in this tree.**
#
# **CONTAINMENT.** Storage cells 555 -> 611: **0 keys lost, 56 added (the entire `_sel_` family and
# nothing else - checked, no added key lacks the prefix), 534 identical, 21 moved**, and every one of the
# 21 is a free-running quantity (poll counts, tick counts, the two absolute power-IRQ timestamps, the
# three `_*_cmdlow_seen` poll indices) or an address inside the entry image (`_pwr_irq_reg_handler`
# 0x8000d314 -> 0x8000d320, which grew). **Not one decision cell moved**: `_cmd1_resp = 0x40ff8080`,
# `_cid_gate_word = 0xc0ff8080`, `_nidx_resp = 0x00000500`, `_nidx_state = 2`, `_csd_structure = 3`,
# `_csd_mmca_vsn = 4` and `_csd_capacity_blocks = 0x00200000` are identical across both boots. Whole-log
# cells 1,467 -> 1,525. The OS came up exactly as 818 measured: `BSD root: md0, major 2, minor 0`, the
# init load returned, pid 1's AST put it in user mode, and the kernel's idle path entered 63,333 times
# (818's count was 62,283 - a free-running number). The run ended on the ladder's own deadline:
# `_post_end_calls = 8`, `_seam_post_end_ticks = 0x06ddd000 = 115,200,000`, `_post_cntfrq = 0x0124f800`
# = 19,200,000 -> **6.0000 s**, and `fault_addr=0xfa0065c` is the known forced ending
# (`mi4-the-run-ends-at-entry-epilogue`). **Nothing on the device changed**: `fastboot boot` only, and
# CMD7 added no store to any device - its whole surface is four reads of `RESPONSE`, the `INT_ENABLE`
# window read-written twice, `SIGNAL_ENABLE`, `INT_STATUS`, the `TIMEOUT_CONTROL` byte (still 0x00, which
# no rung has ever written) and `PRESENT_STATE`, all registers the arms below it already touch.
#
# **WHAT FOLLOWS: CMD13 `SEND_STATUS` IS THE RECOMMENDED NEXT RUNG, AND NOT CMD8.** The frontier is no
# longer CMD7's mechanism or the INDEX bit - it is ONE FIELD'S SAMPLING CONVENTION, and it has a direct
# measurement: a command whose own answer is `R1_CURRENT_STATE`, with no data phase and no state change.
# CMD13 is `mmc_ops.c`'s own `mmc_send_status`, it returns R1 through the same 48-bit path CMD7 just
# proved works, and it needs NO NEW MECHANISM. CMD8 (`SEND_EXT_CSD`, the driver's own next statement at
# `mmc.c:1446`) needs a 512-byte DATA read - no `sdhci_prepare_data`, no block size, no DMA or PIO path,
# and `TIMEOUT_CONTROL` never raised - so **CMD8 is where this ladder stops being a command ladder**, and
# this press does not change that.
#
# **AND A RUNG-21 QUESTION NOW WORTH A RUNG OF ITS OWN**: with `_sel_err = 0` beside the INDEX bit
# enabled, the bit is measured SAFE on a live chain, so putting it back on **CMD3** would give this
# ladder an attributable CMD3 as well - a change with a measured precedent rather than one inherited from
# a dead chain. It is NOT what rung 37 should do: one rung moves one thing.
#
# **THE ARM IS SPENT AND NOTHING IS ARMED.** Its park stays in `out/stage90/frozen/armed-storage-18b0ccf3/`
# because a park is the record of what was built - `frozen/` is a record and NOT a queue, and

# **THE GOAL IS NOT MET.** 「把基础驱动跑起来」 moved again - the storage chain now has an ATTRIBUTABLE
